a62.speaker: Thomas Homan, Trump's "immigration tsar" (acting ICE director in Trump's first term)
a62.name: Thomas Homan
a62.title: Trump's "immigration tsar" (acting ICE director in Trump's first term)
a62.speech: "I will run the biggest deportation force this country has ever seen," Homan said at a conservative conference in July.

a62.speaker: Mike Waltz, Florida Congressman, Trump's pick for national security adviser
a62.name: Mike Waltz
a62.title: Florida Congressman, Trump's pick for national security adviser
a62.speech: Has said the US is in a "cold war" with China and was one of the first members of Congress to call for a US boycott of the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics.

a62.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a62.name: Donald Trump
a62.title: US President-elect
a62.speech: Said cost was not an issue for his mass deportation plan: "When people have killed and murdered, when drug lords have destroyed countries, and now they're going to go back to those countries because they're not staying here," he said. "There is no price tag."

a62.speaker: Elise Stefanik, Trump's pick for US ambassador to the UN
a62.name: Elise Stefanik
a62.title: Trump's pick for US ambassador to the UN
a62.speech: Accused China of "blatant and malicious election interference" amid reports that China-backed hackers attempted to gather information from the former president's phones.

a62.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a62.name: Donald Trump
a62.title: US President-elect
a62.speech: "He wants to do some things, and we're going to let him go to it," Trump said in his election victory speech, referring to Robert F Kennedy Jr's prospective role.

a62.speaker: Some of Trump's advisers, including Elon Musk
a62.name: Some of Trump's advisers
a62.title: including Elon Musk
a62.speech: Warned that the president-elect could be endangering his legislative agenda if he plucks too many more Republicans from the chambers.

a133.speaker: Abdoul Karim Thiombiano, head of the TIN FII project
a133.name: Abdoul Karim Thiombiano
a133.title: head of the TIN FII project
a133.speech: Said: “If you train people, you must equip them with material” ; “we are happy and satisfied with the way this project has unfolded. He is moreover pleading with this fund so that other projects or initiatives may be supported in this direction because in the field the need is immense” ; “this made it possible to revive hope and to give new direction to certain families and certain households, and to create new sources of income for them.”

a133.speaker: Abdoul Karim Thiombiano, head of the TIN FII project
a133.name: Abdoul Karim Thiombiano
a133.title: head of the TIN FII project
a133.speech: Maintains that within the framework of the project, and in order to make the gains achieved sustainable, “they have worked to develop a networking system that consists of organising these girls and young women into a simplified cooperative society so that these girls and young women are more competitive and able to benefit from micro-credit from financial institutions, because increasingly technical and financial partners only support structured actors.”

a133.speaker: Abdou Karim Thiombiano, in charge of the PISCA support fund for innovative projects of civil society and coalitions of actors within the TODI YABA association
a133.name: Abdou Karim Thiombiano
a133.title: in charge of the PISCA support fund for innovative projects of civil society and coalitions of actors within the TODI YABA association
a133.speech: States: “This project is a first in the Eastern region through the support fund for innovative projects of civil society and coalitions of actors (PISCA). All the beneficiaries are delighted by the initiative that was conceived by the TODI YABA association.”

a133.speaker: Thiombiano/Toguyeni Possibo Jocelyne, beneficiary of a knitting kit
a133.name: Thiombiano/Toguyeni Possibo Jocelyne
a133.title: beneficiary of a knitting kit
a133.speech: States with joy “that it is first of all an act of thanksgiving because I am benefiting from these tools offered by the TODI YABA association through the TIN FII project. With this knitting machine I can now do in one week work that used to take me a month. I therefore wish to thank the TODI YABA association from the bottom of my heart for this training and for this equipment acquired. In our turn too, we will share this acquired knowledge with other people who have not received it. We wish the TODI YABA association long life.”

a133.speaker: Other beneficiaries of the TIN FII project
a133.name: Other beneficiaries of the TIN FII project
a133.speech: Say they would like to have working capital and also support for the host families that take them in.

a164.speaker: Concordant witness accounts (local residents)
a164.name: Concordant witness accounts (local residents)
a164.speech: According to concordant testimonies, several shops as well as their contents were entirely destroyed by the flames.

a164.speaker: A local authority (anonymous)
a164.name: A local authority (anonymous)
a164.speech: According to a local official, a short circuit is said to be the cause of the disaster.

a164.speaker: Monsieur Baldé, one of the victims
a164.name: Monsieur Baldé
a164.title: one of the victims
a164.speech: "We were taken by surprise by a fire, and the flames spread quickly, consuming our goods and the buildings."

a209.speaker: Beninese public / listeners (testimonies)
a209.name: Beninese public / listeners (testimonies)
a209.speech: "He is an artist steeped in talent. He is a Beninese star in the making. With support, he will be a complete musician artist like certain great figures of African music." ; "All the songs, added to the rhythms performed, are evocative and draw everyone's attention to the advantages of Beninese culture. This new album by Fifido is a rich cocktail for the greats." ; According to the testimonies gathered, this artist now known to the Beninese public is full of talent and deserves support.

a209.speaker: Fifido (Fidele Dovenon), Beninese artist, creator of the "Tchemin" rhythm
a209.name: Fifido (Fidele Dovenon)
a209.title: Beninese artist, creator of the "Tchemin" rhythm
a209.speech: Said that all these descriptions are no illusion since he took all his time to prepare this record ; Said the album "Vrais amis", which addresses several themes of life including love, courage and hope in God, is the fruit of several years of hard work ; Said that for him culture is the driving force of all development, and that much more is to come from him in the promotion of his country's culture ; "I ask all people of goodwill to come and support what I am doing."

a240.speaker: Tanzania HIV Impact Survey 2022-2023 (THIS 2022-2023) report
a240.name: Tanzania HIV Impact Survey 2022-2023 (THIS 2022-2023) report
a240.speech: Indicates that HIV incidence among girls has doubled to 15.25 percent; HIV prevalence among adults aged 15 and above is 4.5 percent, with women constituting 5.6 percent and men only 3 percent; among people living with HIV, 33 percent are youth aged 15 to 24, of whom 78 percent are girls; the final report, released in September 2024, indicates a decline in HIV incidence among men of all ages; new cases among adults have declined by 16.7 percent, from 72,000 (THIS 2016-2017) to 60,000; Njombe has the highest prevalence at 12.7 percent, followed by Iringa (11.1 percent), Mbeya (9.6 percent), and Songwe (6.0 percent), while Kigoma (1.7 percent) and Manyara (1.8 percent) are lowest, with Pemba North at 0.2 percent, Pemba South at 0.5 percent, Unguja North at 0.7 percent, Mjini Magharibi at 0.4 percent, and Unguja South at 0.8 percent; and shows a decline in condom use during sex.

a240.speaker: Dr. Samuel Sumba, researcher with the Tanzania Commission for AIDS (TACAIDS)
a240.name: Dr. Samuel Sumba
a240.title: researcher with the Tanzania Commission for AIDS (TACAIDS)
a240.speech: Quoting the THIS 2022-2023 report, stated that Tanzania has approximately 1.6 million people living with HIV.

a240.speaker: Dr. Catherine Joachim, acting director of TACAIDS
a240.name: Dr. Catherine Joachim
a240.title: acting director of TACAIDS
a240.speech: Explains that youth engage in sexual activity earlier, prompting the commission to collaborate with the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training to craft HIV awareness messages targeting primary and secondary school students ; "I was shocked to hear what these children were talking about. They know about sex, different styles, and openly discuss these topics—even in front of religious leaders—without fear." ; encouraged researchers to develop solutions for effectively reaching this group with appropriate messages to curb the spread of HIV/AIDS.

a240.speaker: Dr. Catherine Joachim, acting director of TACAIDS
a240.name: Dr. Catherine Joachim
a240.title: acting director of TACAIDS
a240.speech: Highlighted government efforts to ensure free condom distribution at public places, such as offices and bus stops, with branded condoms sold at discounted prices ; "Condoms are being distributed in public places using dispensers, and they are taken quickly. However, we are hearing that condom usage during sex has decreased. Researchers should investigate why people take condoms but fail to use them as a preventive measure."

a240.speaker: Peter Masika, CEO and founder of the Tanzania Youth Alliance (TAYOA)
a240.name: Peter Masika
a240.title: CEO and founder of the Tanzania Youth Alliance (TAYOA)
a240.speech: Urged researchers to investigate whether behavioral factors contribute to the significant differences in prevalence between regions with similar environmental conditions, specifically citing Njombe and Kigoma, where girls face similar challenges, including economic hardship and agricultural engagement, yet their HIV prevalence rates differ.

a240.speaker: Dr. Ezekiel Luoga, researcher with the Ifakara Health Institute (IHI)
a240.name: Dr. Ezekiel Luoga
a240.title: researcher with the Ifakara Health Institute (IHI)
a240.speech: Emphasized improving HIV-related information systems and their proper use to enhance service provision ; "Most health practitioners do not use data to improve services," stressing the importance of education in addressing HIV challenges.

a240.speaker: Omary Ilyas, Prime Minister's Office (PMO)
a240.name: Omary Ilyas
a240.title: Prime Minister's Office (PMO)
a240.speech: Noted that researchers and academics have the opportunity to guide the government toward achieving independent health services as part of the country's Agenda 2050 ; "Without a healthy society, we cannot achieve our plans for the next 25 years." ; called for better performance monitoring of workshops and the preparation of a matrix outlining priorities, responsibilities, and timelines for implementation.

a240.speaker: TACAIDS Strategic Plan (document)
a240.name: TACAIDS Strategic Plan (document)
a240.speech: Outlines effective strategies to coordinate and manage the national HIV/AIDS response, aiming to meet the 95-95-95 targets and end AIDS by 2030, aligning closely with the Third Five-Year Development Plan (FYDP III) 2021/22–2025/26.

a240.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice President of Tanzania
a240.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a240.title: Vice President of Tanzania
a240.speech: Praised Tanzania's progress in the fight against HIV/AIDS during the National World AIDS Day celebrations in Songea, Ruvuma Region, on December 1, 2024 ; "These results show significant progress toward our goal of ending HIV/AIDS by 2030." ; highlighted the global 95-95-95 targets for 2025, urging TACAIDS to collaborate with sector ministries, stakeholders, and communities to address factors driving HIV spread ; commended partnerships with stakeholders, including the private sector, the Global Fund, PEPFAR, and UN agencies, for supporting HIV/AIDS programs in Tanzania.

a240.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice President of Tanzania
a240.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a240.title: Vice President of Tanzania
a240.speech: Urged young people, especially girls, to protect themselves from new infections and embrace education campaigns promoting behavioral change and the abandonment of harmful cultural practices ; "The new infections are often driven by risky behaviors such as excessive alcohol consumption, unprotected sex, multiple partners, and drug abuse." ; called for eliminating stigma around people living with HIV, noting that stigma prevents many from accessing vital services like voluntary testing, counseling, and ART.

a240.speaker: Leticia Maurice, Chairperson of the National Council of People Living with HIV
a240.name: Leticia Maurice
a240.title: Chairperson of the National Council of People Living with HIV
a240.speech: Called for the elimination of stigma and drug abuse, which hinder the government's efforts to fight the scourge, and reaffirmed the council's commitment to strengthening services tailored to the needs of vulnerable groups.

a372.speaker: 2022 population and housing census (Tanzania)
a372.name: 2022 population and housing census (Tanzania)
a372.speech: According to the census, Tanzania has a total of 21.3 million people aged between 15 and 35.

a372.speaker: Stakeholders (wadau)
a372.name: Stakeholders (wadau)
a372.speech: Say an increase in new HIV infections, sexually transmitted diseases, teenage pregnancies and maternal deaths should be expected because of the absence of the aid.

a372.speaker: Hadija Maganga, youth leader and peer educator
a372.name: Hadija Maganga
a372.title: youth leader and peer educator
a372.speech: Said access to reproductive health services and commodities for young people and young women in the country is essential for the well-being of society, especially in this period of changes in foreign aid policies; said adolescent girls are severely affected by the lack of information, especially on reproductive health. “At this time, when we hear reports that aid is coming to an end, as stakeholders we are left asking ourselves what the situation will be like. When you talk to adolescents they clearly show that there is secrecy within families – parents do not speak openly with them about reproductive health matters.” ; “Many look for information themselves; peer educators helped a great deal, and we are not sure whether the government will be able to do what USAID did.” ; Added that the government should seek solutions for reproductive health, especially for adolescents: “The government cannot place the emphasis in the way the SHARP projects do to ensure that young people are involved.”

a372.speaker: Denis Bwana, reproductive health expert
a372.name: Denis Bwana
a372.title: reproductive health expert
a372.speech: Said the availability of these services is the correct answer to tackling teenage pregnancies in regions with high numbers, including Manyara and Morogoro, especially access to family planning services. “Reproductive health services include family planning matters, the use of condoms and similar medical supplies; they contribute greatly to tackling the challenge of teenage pregnancies.” ; Said teenage pregnancies are directly linked to child marriage, because reproductive health services include the delivery of accurate information, which helps girls make their own decisions, and that such information contributes greatly to reducing HIV infections. “Within it there was a variety of health advocacy; there were community-level service providers who went around providing education to peer groups, through programmes that were under USAID funding and that helped to tackle these challenges. With these projects halted, these young people will not be able to get much information. The remaining programmes are not enough, and even when the USAID ones existed they were still insufficient – the meaning of this is that young people will be at risk of infection, teenage pregnancies will increase, and child marriages too.” ; Said many teenage pregnancies contribute to maternal and newborn deaths, because the child will be born to a mother who is not ready economically, biologically, psychologically or mentally, and that the harm occurring now could affect future generations.

a372.speaker: Denis Bwana, reproductive health expert
a372.name: Denis Bwana
a372.title: reproductive health expert
a372.speech: Says the country needs to assess how it used the aid provided through USAID, how many experts were produced and what they can do for the country now, and that there must be accountability. “In order to be able to restore these services, we must relax the conditions so that there is a friendly environment – taxes; if our policies are not friendly people will leave, so we must review our policies so that the private sector can invest in health.” ; Stressed that it is important to be innovative in investing in the health sector. “We have done something good in maternal and child services, but our health systems will be stuck if we depend more on aid. Because we did not invest in health, all the foreign aid from the United States is little money, but look at its impact on us. This is where we should see the importance of our taxes: the first investment should be in health, second education and infrastructure. Reproductive health has been shaken more at present. We must have health systems that are sustainable.”

a372.speaker: Reverend Modest Pesha, Coordinator of the Christian Council of Tanzania (CCT)
a372.name: Reverend Modest Pesha
a372.title: Coordinator of the Christian Council of Tanzania (CCT)
a372.speech: Said it is still early to assess the effects on youth groups within the short period of the changes in foreign aid policies; said access to reproductive health services and commodities for those groups is important in targeting HIV infections, teenage pregnancies, unintended pregnancies and forced marriages resulting from teenage pregnancies, and would help reduce maternal and child deaths, especially among those giving birth at a young age, in order to reach the SDG targets, as well as conflicts in households and communities and the break-up of families. “Services concerning reproductive health include providing education starting at the family level, with parents breaking the silence, together with religious institutions incorporating reproductive health education into their teachings.” ; Stressed that the availability of commodities should take into account ethics, principles and religious teachings, age and proper use, in order to avoid further harm.

a372.speaker: Stakeholders (wadau)
a372.name: Stakeholders (wadau)
a372.speech: Have called on the government to ensure it fulfils various agreements, including the Abuja agreement, which requires countries to allocate 15 percent of their budget to health.

a372.speaker: Dr Grace Magembe, Chief Medical Officer of the Government of Tanzania
a372.name: Dr Grace Magembe
a372.title: Chief Medical Officer of the Government of Tanzania
a372.speech: Said the matter is being handled by a team from the Prime Minister's Office, who are looking at all those services, and a report will be issued after analysis; said no service has stopped, that services are continuing having been integrated together, and that ARV and other drugs are being received; however said the group of civil society organisations that were providing education to young people about teenage pregnancies and reproductive health is stopping. “We are looking at how they must continue. At present community-level service providers are there, being paid by the government, and they provide all integrated services, from public education, tuberculosis services, malaria, family planning, teenage pregnancies. We have created an integrated plan in which the community-level service provider has been enabled through special training; it is among the strategies that will give us sustainability of those services, and they also provide education. This is being worked on by a team within the government, not the Ministry of Health alone.” ; Stressed that all essential services, especially those concerning treatment and therapy, are continuing as normal.

a430.speaker: Algerian Ministry of Defence
a430.name: Algerian Ministry of Defence
a430.speech: Announced that four military aircraft took off on 19 August from the Boufarik air base for Niamey airport, carrying food, medicines, medical equipment, as well as tents and mattresses provided by the Algerian Red Crescent ; stated that the gesture corresponds to the "principles of cooperation and humanitarian solidarity with brotherly and friendly countries" and comes in response to "the devastation caused by the recent floods in Niger."

a475.speaker: United Nations official (unnamed, told the BBC)
a475.name: United Nations official (unnamed
a475.title: told the BBC)
a475.speech: Said hundreds of thousands of people are "slowly starving" in Kenyan refugee camps after US funding cuts reduced food rations to their lowest ever levels.

a475.speaker: A medic at Kakuma's Amusait Hospital
a475.name: A medic at Kakuma's Amusait Hospital
a475.speech: Tells the BBC that the wrinkled and peeling skin of baby Hellen, leaving angry patches of red, is the result of malnutrition.

a475.speaker: Agnes Awila, refugee from northern Uganda and mother of baby James
a475.name: Agnes Awila
a475.title: refugee from northern Uganda and mother of baby James
a475.speech: "The food is not enough, my children eat only once a day. If there's no food what do you feed them?"

a475.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a475.name: Donald Trump
a475.title: US President
a475.speech: Announced sweeping cuts to US foreign aid programmes earlier this year, as part of his "America First" policy.

a475.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a475.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a475.speech: Says that as a result of the cuts, the agency has had to slash the refugees' rations to 30% of the minimum recommended amount a person should eat to stay healthy.

a475.speaker: Felix Okech, WFP head of refugee operations in Kenya
a475.name: Felix Okech
a475.title: WFP head of refugee operations in Kenya
a475.speech: "If we have a protracted situation where this is what we can manage, then basically we have a slowly starving population" ; "It is a really dire situation" ; "We do have some signals from some one or two donors about support with that cash component. But remember, the very kind and generous US has been providing over 70% - so if you're still missing 70%… those prospects are not good."

a475.speaker: Mukuniwa Bililo Mami, 51-year-old refugee from South Kivu, DR Congo, mother of two
a475.name: Mukuniwa Bililo Mami
a475.title: 51-year-old refugee from South Kivu, DR Congo, mother of two
a475.speech: "I am grateful to receive this little [food] but it is not enough" ; says the refugees used to "eat well" - three meals a day, but now that rations are at 30% of their usual amount, the food she has been given is not enough to last one month, let alone the two that she has been asked to stretch it for.

a475.speaker: Badaba Ibrahim, 42-year-old refugee trader from the Nuba Mountains, Sudan
a475.name: Badaba Ibrahim
a475.title: 42-year-old refugee trader from the Nuba Mountains, Sudan
a475.speech: Says his customers, now unable to purchase food, at times camp at his shop all day, begging for help: "They will tell you, 'My children have not eaten for a full day.'"

a475.speaker: Agnes Livio, 28-year-old refugee from South Sudan, mother of five
a475.name: Agnes Livio
a475.title: 28-year-old refugee from South Sudan, mother of five
a475.speech: "We used to get porridge for breakfast but not anymore. So, the children have to wait until the afternoon to have their first meal."

a527.speaker: Dr. Edward Lama Wonkeryor, Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a527.name: Dr. Edward Lama Wonkeryor
a527.title: Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a527.speech: Has reaffirmed the Government of Liberia's commitment to collaborating with the USAID TESTS Project; speaking on behalf of the government, he highlighted the Boakai administration's dedication to addressing critical issues within the education sector and emphasized that the partnership with the USAID TESTS Project reflects the government's determination to revitalize teacher training programs across Liberia's tertiary institutions ; expressed the government's intent to leverage this partnership to strengthen faculty and leadership development, with a particular focus on early childhood and primary education.

a527.speaker: Dr. Edward Lama Wonkeryor, Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a527.name: Dr. Edward Lama Wonkeryor
a527.title: Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a527.speech: Described the initiative as a significant step toward rebranding the educational landscape in the country, emphasizing its importance for the professional growth of educators: "The demands of a rapidly changing global landscape make it vital for our institutions to cultivate adaptive leaders and skilled educators who can deliver high-quality education and inspire our youth," he said ; "By focusing on the professional development of faculty members and administrators, we are strengthening the foundation upon which our education system stands, aligning our vision with sustainable growth and global competitiveness. The teacher training initiatives under the USAID TESTS Project are critical to enhancing the capacity of our higher education institutions." ; He said it has long been a priority for NCHE to elevate the standard of teacher education across various programs, which aligns with our vision for a stronger education system in Liberia.

a527.speaker: Dr. Edward Lama Wonkeryor, Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a527.name: Dr. Edward Lama Wonkeryor
a527.title: Executive Director of the National Commission on Higher Education (NCHE), Liberia
a527.speech: Further disclosed plans to collaborate with the Ministry of Education to engage the U.S. Government for additional support ; noted the intention of his institution to extend the USAID TESTS Project's benefits to other NCHE-affiliated institutions that were not initially included, underscoring the desire for broader participation in the program.

a730.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chairman of the Party for Democracy and Progress (Chadema), Tanzania
a730.name: Tundu Lissu
a730.title: Chairman of the Party for Democracy and Progress (Chadema), Tanzania
a730.speech: Said that the policy changes being made by US President Donald Trump are a sign that Tanzania should learn to abandon dependence on foreign nations because that situation is dangerous; said that in just the first 30 days of his second term Trump has begun making changes with major consequences, especially in sectors on which Tanzania had depended on aid, such as health, agriculture and road infrastructure ; "We need to learn that dependency is dangerous for a country and even for an individual. When you depend on others, when things happen in those nations, even if they do not concern you directly, they will touch you." ; Stressed that Tanzania must strengthen itself economically to withstand international changes, and clarified that self-reliance does not mean ceasing to cooperate with other nations but having the ability to manage on its own when changes occur ; "It is important to have the capacity to stand on your own for a certain period, although you can never be completely self-reliant all the time, because even big nations like China cannot."

a730.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chairman of the Party for Democracy and Progress (Chadema), Tanzania
a730.name: Tundu Lissu
a730.title: Chairman of the Party for Democracy and Progress (Chadema), Tanzania
a730.speech: Gave the example of USAID, saying the dismantling of the agency within such a short time is a matter with major consequences: "USAID was established in 1961 by President John F. Kennedy as an important step in matters of international relations. It was part of the United States' efforts to help rebuild Europe after the Second World War, and for a long time it has been a great support for developing countries." ; "Now Trump, within one month, has announced the abolition of USAID, an agency with a huge budget running its operations all over the world. In countries like Tanzania, the health sector has benefited for many years from those funds, especially in the fight against AIDS and in major malaria projects." ; Said USAID assistance strengthened not only health but also road infrastructure, citing the tarmac road from Tunduma to Sumbawanga: "The money of the American people is everywhere here in Tanzania, and it is provided through USAID. The abolition of that agency has caused thousands of workers employed through its projects to lose their jobs."

a730.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chairman of the Party for Democracy and Progress (Chadema), Tanzania
a730.name: Tundu Lissu
a730.title: Chairman of the Party for Democracy and Progress (Chadema), Tanzania
a730.speech: Said Trump is doing things no other leader of his stature has ever done: "I know the history of the United States and its presidents to a certain extent. There is no other President like Trump who is making such major changes in terms of foreign policy; perhaps we would have to go back to the era of that nation's founders such as George Washington, John Adams and Thomas Jefferson, who held the position of not wanting the United States to get involved in Europe's conflicts." ; Said the voice of those founders is heard through Trump's policies, which put American interests first and withdraw from European affairs; said that for the first time Trump has announced that responsibility for Europe's defence and security should remain with those nations themselves ; On Ukraine and Russia, said Trump claims he will end the war because without American military support Ukraine will not be able to continue: "Without the United States declaring Ukraine a member of the NATO defence alliance in 2008, the situation would have been different. Now Trump says he is ending that war." ; Said European nations are going through a great shock because the nation that had helped them for many years is now withdrawing ; "The United States has been the most powerful nation in the world since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991. For more than 30 years, the world has been under the rule of the United States as the only powerful nation, although now China is an economically very powerful nation and is increasingly doing more trade than the United States." ; "When the economy is big, even military power comes close behind. However, Russia too has returned to its prime, and the proof is the war in Ukraine, in which it has fought against the whole of NATO and been able to withstand the attacks."

a730.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a730.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a730.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a730.speech: Speaking in Parliament on February 6, 2025, addressed the policy changes and stressed that the Government of Tanzania has organised itself to build a self-reliant economy: "It is true that our government respects foreign policy and we implement agreements in accordance with the accords with the countries concerned. However, we have begun to see changes in the policies of some very powerful countries such as the United States, and these changes could affect various nations, including Tanzania."

a1008.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a1008.name: Donald Trump
a1008.title: US President-elect
a1008.speech: He promised to tackle a range of domestic issues, including immigration and inflation, and signalled a return to his 'America First' foreign policy; he made bold claims about his ability to end Russia's war against Ukraine within 24 hours of taking office, bring peace to the Middle East, and assert dominance over China.

a1008.speaker: Tuliameni Kalomoh, seasoned diplomat and former Namibian ambassador
a1008.name: Tuliameni Kalomoh
a1008.title: seasoned diplomat and former Namibian ambassador
a1008.speech: Said yesterday that there is no need to lose sleep over the future relationship between Namibia and the United States and that it will remain largely unchanged: "Our relationship with the Americans will not change. In terms of trade, we sell them diamonds. We will sell them uranium and other commodities. I do not think that will be disrupted, because it's in their interest. They provide us very generous financial support towards the United States President's Emergency Plan For AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)."

a1008.speaker: Tuliameni Kalomoh, seasoned diplomat and former Namibian ambassador
a1008.name: Tuliameni Kalomoh
a1008.title: seasoned diplomat and former Namibian ambassador
a1008.speech: "We all remember that Trump had recognised the Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara. It was tragic. The other fundamental foreign policy interest for Namibia is Palestine. Now, Trump had recognised Israeli sovereignty over East Jerusalem, and they moved the American embassy from Tehran to East Jerusalem, calling Jerusalem the eternal capital of the Jewish state," he recalled ; he also said Trump recognised Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights, the Syrian territory Israel captured during the 1967 war: "Mind you, there is a provision in international law that no territory can be acquired using force. But Trump, with the gradual government in Israel, ignored that international law."

a1008.speaker: Tuliameni Kalomoh, seasoned diplomat and former Namibian ambassador
a1008.name: Tuliameni Kalomoh
a1008.title: seasoned diplomat and former Namibian ambassador
a1008.speech: "For Namibia's interest, it's the vexing trade and financial blockade of Cuba. More than 60 years old. And Obama had relaxed some of the sanctions; Trump came to power, reimposed such sanctions, and introduced additional ones. This causes unbearable suffering and economic dislocation in Cuba. When (Joe) Biden came to power, he did nothing to reverse any one of those policies Trump introduced."

a1008.speaker: Kaire Mbuende, politician and former Namibian diplomat
a1008.name: Kaire Mbuende
a1008.title: politician and former Namibian diplomat
a1008.speech: Said that even after the popular vote, there is an electoral college, and the result could be different: "These two candidates are focusing on similar issues: abortion and issues of immigration, because their foreign policy may be the same. But for the American people, it's a big difference. That is why we are seeing a higher level of participation than usual."

a1008.speaker: Kaire Mbuende, politician and former Namibian diplomat
a1008.name: Kaire Mbuende
a1008.title: politician and former Namibian diplomat
a1008.speech: Said what is strange for him is that Africans featured nowhere significantly during the US presidential campaigns: "The fact that Africa doesn't feature prominently in the election campaign is a blessing in disguise" ; "It's good because then they will allow Africans to shape their own agenda. And when we, as Africans, engage the US, we will engage them on our terms, in terms of our understanding of our reality."

a1008.speaker: Kaire Mbuende, politician and former Namibian diplomat
a1008.name: Kaire Mbuende
a1008.title: politician and former Namibian diplomat
a1008.speech: "President Obama expressed himself that it's about time to lift sanctions against Cuba. And that means the victory for the Democrats. We may see a relaxation of American policy towards Cuba, an opening, a greater opening; whereas the Trump administration will see the same halt in terms of relations to Cuba, in terms of relations on the question of Palestine," he observed.

a1017.speaker: Augushito Davite, 69, and Patricia Lemeti, 42, Mozambican asylum seekers speaking on behalf of other asylum seekers at Nyamithuthu camp
a1017.name: Augushito Davite
a1017.title: 69, and Patricia Lemeti, 42, Mozambican asylum seekers speaking on behalf of other asylum seekers at Nyamithuthu camp
a1017.speech: Said the lack of food assistance is their most urgent need: "We are starving, the support being rendered is mostly non-food items."

a1017.speaker: Hilda Katema, senior administrative and operations manager, Department for Refugees (Malawi)
a1017.name: Hilda Katema
a1017.title: senior administrative and operations manager, Department for Refugees (Malawi)
a1017.speech: Acknowledged the crisis and assured that the government is committed to addressing the food needs of the asylum seekers.

a1017.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Commissioner of Malawi's Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA)
a1017.name: Charles Kalemba
a1017.title: Commissioner of Malawi's Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA)
a1017.speech: Confirmed that his department, in collaboration with the Department for Refugees, is working to ensure that the asylum seekers at Nyamithuthu camp receive essential supplies, including food, and emphasized the department's role in managing large numbers of people in camps and providing necessary expertise.

a1017.speaker: Gloria Nyang'iye, Associate Reporting Officer for UNHCR
a1017.name: Gloria Nyang'iye
a1017.title: Associate Reporting Officer for UNHCR
a1017.speech: Highlighted the progress in improving the camp's shelter and sanitation facilities, ensuring a more stable environment for the asylum seekers.

a1032.speaker: Fassou Théa, Guinean Minister of Fisheries and the Maritime Economy
a1032.name: Fassou Théa
a1032.title: Guinean Minister of Fisheries and the Maritime Economy
a1032.speech: welcomed a “strategic” support for the Guinean fisheries sector: “These inspection kits are not simply logistical equipment. They constitute a genuine strategic added value in the service of health and health security. Thanks to this support, ONSPA will be able to effectively fulfil its sovereign mission in accordance with national and international standards.”

a1032.speaker: Dr Mamadou Bano Diallo, Director General of ONSPA
a1032.name: Dr Mamadou Bano Diallo
a1032.title: Director General of ONSPA
a1032.speech: recalled the central role of his institution in protecting public health and promoting Guinean exports: “ONSPA works tirelessly to guarantee the quality and health compliance of fishery and aquaculture products intended for local consumption and for export. The success of this mission depends largely on the availability of appropriate logistical and human resources.” ; “ONSPA will make good use of this equipment in a spirit of responsibility and efficiency, in order to strengthen the health safety of fishery products and the competitiveness of our exports.”

a1032.speaker: Dr Moustapha Grovogui, National Coordinator of the Regional Health Security Programme
a1032.name: Dr Moustapha Grovogui
a1032.title: National Coordinator of the Regional Health Security Programme
a1032.speech: stressed the need for continuous strengthening of institutional capacities to prevent health risks in the food sector: “Our country faces multiple and simultaneous epidemics. This programme aims to strengthen human, animal and environmental health within an integrated ‘One Health’ approach.”

a1147.speaker: The kidnappers (Greenfield University abduction)
a1147.name: The kidnappers (Greenfield University abduction)
a1147.speech: Three days later, on Friday, 23 April, the kidnappers told parents that they had a message for them: the remains of Dorathy Yohanna, Precious Nwakacha and Sadiq Yusuf Sanga were left on the side of a road.

a1147.speaker: Sadiq Yusuf Sanga, third-year cyber security student, Greenfield University
a1147.name: Sadiq Yusuf Sanga
a1147.title: third-year cyber security student, Greenfield University
a1147.speech: Woke the morning he was killed to share his dream: three people were going home and he was one of them.

a1147.speaker: Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria
a1147.name: Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria
a1147.speech: "the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government".

a1147.speaker: Dike Chukwumerijie, spoken word and performance poet
a1147.name: Dike Chukwumerijie
a1147.title: spoken word and performance poet
a1147.speech: Wrote a poem for the campaign, 'how much blood will this land drink before we say enough'.

a1147.speaker: Anthea Lawson, author of Entangled Activist
a1147.name: Anthea Lawson
a1147.title: author of Entangled Activist
a1147.speech: Theorises that, "activists are part of and injured by and survivors of the very problems that we are trying to change in the world and our tactics and organisations often mirror the same frameworks for operating that we say we want to change. Some of that entails how we center ourselves as subjects and see those we are trying to help (with our superior knowledge) as objects".

a1147.speaker: Professor Issa Shivji, author of Silences in NGO Discourse
a1147.name: Professor Issa Shivji
a1147.title: author of Silences in NGO Discourse
a1147.speech: Identifies NGOs as handmaidens of a neo-liberal purpose i.e., replacing a degraded state no longer charged with social goods and welfare and pretending to be 'pro poor' while maintaining the capitalist, globalisation hegemony ; Accuses activists of trying to change the world without understanding it: 'How can you make poverty history without understanding the history of poverty', he asks ; Observes that NGOs ignore geopolitical realities, and, with Lawson, notes that the politics of aid and funding create dependencies and, in some cases, make it harder for people and institutions to collaborate ; Is right about paying attention to existing power structures around which societies are organised.

a1147.speaker: Almut Rochowanski, Rethinking Foreign Aid
a1147.name: Almut Rochowanski
a1147.title: Rethinking Foreign Aid
a1147.speech: "Money is never just money. It is power incarnate."

a1147.speaker: President of the Catholic Women's Organization (CWO)
a1147.name: President of the Catholic Women's Organization (CWO)
a1147.speech: 'I hope our sisters in the north have joined', the CWO's president said to me the first time we spoke.

a1147.speaker: Nigeria's National Bureau of Statistics
a1147.name: Nigeria's National Bureau of Statistics
a1147.speech: Reported recently that between May 2023 and April 2024, 2.2 million Nigerians were kidnapped, over half a million were killed by kidnappers and N2.2 trillion ($1.4 billion) paid as ransom.

a1147.speaker: Unnamed participant in WhatsApp groups
a1147.name: Unnamed participant in WhatsApp groups
a1147.speech: 'Let women lead the charge', someone said.

a1147.speaker: Security analysts reports
a1147.name: Security analysts reports
a1147.speech: Deduced that kidnapping funds other transnational organized crime.

a1147.speaker: Ayisha Osori, author of Love Does Not Win Elections (op-ed author)
a1147.name: Ayisha Osori
a1147.title: author of Love Does Not Win Elections (op-ed author)
a1147.speech: Argues that the recent suspension of USAID puts aid politics in focus, noting that as one of Africa's major recipients of U.S. foreign aid, estimated at $1.02 billion in 2023 alone, the suspension has sparked debates in Nigeria about the politics of aid, with positions ranging from blaming international aid for dulling and dissipating civic dissent and lowering citizens' expectations of government, to aid being a form of repayment of the debt owed from colonialism, neocolonialism and neoliberalism, while others point out that the US is the biggest beneficiary of its aid — in 2017, 60 per cent of USAID funding went to 25 US organisations.

a1297.speaker: Abdelmadjid Tebboune, President of Algeria (message delivered by emissary)
a1297.name: Abdelmadjid Tebboune
a1297.title: President of Algeria (message delivered by emissary)
a1297.speech: The message handed to the Head of State concerns an official invitation from President Tebboune inviting his Djiboutian counterpart to take part in the 31st general meeting of the League of Arab States, which will be held next November in Algeria.

a1297.speaker: Kamal Rezig, Algerian Minister of Trade and Export Promotion, and Mohamed Warsama Dirieh, his Djiboutian counterpart
a1297.name: Kamal Rezig
a1297.title: Algerian Minister of Trade and Export Promotion, and Mohamed Warsama Dirieh, his Djiboutian counterpart
a1297.speech: At the end of the audience, they spoke to the Djiboutian press. They indicated in their remarks that the meeting provided a framework for discussing ways and means of increasing the level of exchange and cooperation between the two countries and the two brotherly peoples — in particular the merits of setting up a joint parity commission between the two countries, whose mission would be to define projects of shared economic interest for the two nations.

a1349.speaker: UNICEF (U.N. children's agency)
a1349.name: UNICEF (U.N. children's agency)
a1349.speech: Said on Tuesday that funding cuts are driving an entire generation of children in Sudan to the brink of irreversible harm as support is scaled back and malnutrition cases persist across the country. ; Said children were being cut off from life-saving services due to funding cuts, while the scale of need is staggering. ; Said access to areas in need also continues to be a challenge, with some roads rendered inaccessible due to the rainy season, hampering aid delivery efforts, and that other areas continue to be under siege, such as Al-Fashir.

a1349.speaker: Sheldon Yett, UNICEF's Representative in Sudan
a1349.name: Sheldon Yett
a1349.title: UNICEF's Representative in Sudan
a1349.speech: "Children have limited access to safe water, food, healthcare. Malnutrition is rife, and many good children are reduced to just skin, bones," speaking via video link from Port Sudan. ; "With recent funding cuts, many of our partners in Khartoum and elsewhere have been forced to scale back… We are being stretched to the limit across Sudan, with children dying of hunger." ; "We on the verge of irreversible damage being done to an entire generation of children in Sudan."

a1349.speaker: World Food Programme
a1349.name: World Food Programme
a1349.speech: Said in July that several areas to the south of Sudan's capital Khartoum are at risk of famine.

a1349.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1349.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1349.speech: According to OCHA, only 23% of the 4.16 billion dollar global humanitarian response plan for Sudan has been funded.

a1349.speaker: Jens Laerke, OCHA
a1349.name: Jens Laerke
a1349.title: OCHA
a1349.speech: "It has been one year since famine was confirmed in ZamZam camp and no food has reached this area. Al-Fashir remains under siege. We need that access now."

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (Annual Message to the 55th Legislature)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (Annual Message to the 55th Legislature)
a1618.speech: Said the country now faces a MOMENT OF TRUTH in which democracy can be threatened by those who oppose steady progress: "I assure you that the security of the state and the sanctity of our Republic, though may be assailed, may be threatened; however, it can never be broken. It will be preserved." ; "No one's personal ambition can ever outweigh the importance of our peace and security! This rescue train is moving, and I urge those harboring mental reservations to hop on board and let us proceed with the business of the Liberian people together."

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on the legislative agenda)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on the legislative agenda)
a1618.speech: Commended legislators for passing eleven legislations and one joint resolution and urged them to act swiftly on outstanding proposals - the Presidential Transition Bill, the National Tourism Bill, the Local Government Bill, the Bank-Financial Institutions Act of 2024 and the new Zoning Law - announcing new proposals including the Liberia Youth Service Program (LYSEP), the TVET Commission Act of 2024, the Amended Payment Systems Act, the Liberia Insurance Regulatory Commission Act, the Revised Code of Conduct for Public Officials and the State-Owned Enterprises Authority of Liberia (SEAL), and warned that delays in acting on them could jeopardize the success of the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on the state of the economy)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on the state of the economy)
a1618.speech: Said the administration inherited an economy in steep decline, with growth slowed to 4.6 percent, inflation at 10.1 percent, a current account deficit of 26.4 percent of GDP, reserves at 2.1 months of import cover and debt of $2.5 billion, or 54.6 percent of GDP; reported that in 2024 the economy grew at a revised real rate of 5.1%, inflation was reduced to 7.7%, international reserves improved to US$458.9 million, the Liberian dollar appreciated by 4.7%, the monetary policy rate was cut from 20% to 17%, private sector credit rose 9.1%, and that growth of 5.8% is anticipated in 2025; announced that the 2025 national budget of US$880.7 million was passed before the start of the fiscal year for the first time in the post-war period, that domestic revenue collection reached $695.3 million, a 12% growth and the highest in the nation's history, and that VAT was introduced in April 2024 to replace the outdated Goods and Services Tax.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on relations with bilateral and multilateral partners)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on relations with bilateral and multilateral partners)
a1618.speech: Said his Government has worked tirelessly to rebuild trust with international financial institutions and the donor community, securing a US$210 million package from the IMF's Extended Credit Facility for 2024 to 2027; reported that the World Bank provided $60 million (US$40 million budget support, US$20 million to a Special Disaster Fund) and pledged $40 million in budget support for this year and 2026, that Liberia secured a $60 million grant from the European Union for 2025-2027 and $40 million from the African Development Bank for road projects, and that Liberia received $398.2 million in off-budget Official Development Assistance for health, agriculture and infrastructure; and announced a commitment from the Government of the United States for Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Compact eligibility, reflecting confidence in the steps Liberia is taking in promoting transparency, sound economic decisions and strengthened governance.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on the national development plan)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on the national development plan)
a1618.speech: Reported that the national development plan and fifteen County Development Agendas were developed, validated and launched on January 15, 2025 as the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID), built on the Pro-Poor Agenda for Prosperity and Development and the Agenda for Transformation, and said the total estimated cost of the plan is $8.4 billion, of which 60 percent of the funding will come from the government and international donors, with the remainder from private investment.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on agriculture)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on agriculture)
a1618.speech: Said over 4,000 hectares of rice were cultivated to reduce reliance on rice imports, with a target of an additional 6,000 hectares this year, five mechanization centers under construction in Bong, Lofa, Margibi, Montserrado and Nimba counties, over 10,000 hectares of cocoa cultivation, and that his Administration increased the agricultural budget by over 200% compared to previous years, while launching the Comprehensive Food Security and Nutrition Survey to combat food insecurity.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on road infrastructure)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on road infrastructure)
a1618.speech: Said it is unacceptable that out of 13,000 kilometers of the proposed road network only 1,600 kilometers are paved, and reported that 783 kilometers of major roads were maintained nationwide, the RIA Road Project was expanded from 8 to 20 kilometers of paved roadway, the Sanniquellie to Logatuo Road Project is 85% complete and the Saclepea to Tappita Road Project 50% complete, with paving of the Medina to Robertsport road to commence in March.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on education)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on education)
a1618.speech: Said the administration inherited an educational sector with $2 million in scholarship arrears, poorly qualified teachers and inadequate infrastructure, committed $1 million to clear scholarship arrears including WASSCE fees, and launched a $75 million foundational learning project with USAID focusing on reading and math for third graders, equipping 156 public schools with digital learning platforms and solar power, alongside the "One Child, One Chair" initiative and one million United States dollars allocated to the school feeding program.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on health and sanitation)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on health and sanitation)
a1618.speech: Reported that public health centers in all 15 counties received essential medicines, child vaccination rates rose from 64.9% to 73% in 2024, drug and substance abuse was declared a health emergency and a threat to national security, a $16 million National Clinical and Diagnostic Laboratory was broken ground with Chinese Government support, and a Cardiothoracic Center is being established at JFK with the University of Ghana Medical Centre; on sanitation, said 42 percent of the population still lacks basic toilet facilities, that the 1-million-gallon city reservoir in Central Monrovia was repaired with World Bank support, and that with USAID support the Government is conducting the feasibility of rehabilitating the Kakata and Buchanan water systems.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on transparency and anti-corruption)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on transparency and anti-corruption)
a1618.speech: Declared that the "business-as-usual" approach to governance would be a thing of the past, reported that the General Auditing Commission published results for 60 out of 80 audits and that payroll audits across several ministries removed thousands of ghost names, and vowed: "Liberians yearn for decisive action against this national menace, and I vow to deliver!" while calling on the National Legislature and Judiciary to act on audit reports and fast-track corruption cases.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on foreign relations and Liberia's image)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on foreign relations and Liberia's image)
a1618.speech: Announced that Liberia established diplomatic relations with six new countries - Barbados, Bahrain, Uzbekistan, Croatia, El Salvador and Bolivia - signed nine new bilateral agreements with Cote d'Ivoire and fifteen with Morocco, secured a 108 million euro budget envelope from the European Union, launched a bid for a non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council for the 2026-2027 term with African Union and ECOWAS endorsement, and said Liberia stood with Ukraine in protecting its sovereignty and supported a ceasefire in Gaza as well as the return of the UN Agency for Palestine.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (on the Liberian Diaspora)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (on the Liberian Diaspora)
a1618.speech: Recalled telling the body last January that "Liberians in the Diaspora have a stake in the future of their country, and my administration will ensure that their contributions to Liberia are institutionalized and fully harnessed," and announced a new "Annual Year of Return" program and the first Liberia Diaspora Conference on National Development in April 2025 in Washington, DC.

a1618.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., President of Liberia (concluding commitments)
a1618.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1618.title: Sr., President of Liberia (concluding commitments)
a1618.speech: Pledged to propose an action plan to address the state of national unity, a review of the Constitution, comprehensive electoral reforms, plans for the proper burial of former presidents William R. Tolbert and Samuel K. Doe, a plan to recognize ECOWAS, and a National Conference on Post-War Infrastructure, concluding that "After one year in office, we can confidently say that the STATE OF OUR NATION is better than when we began."

a1697.speaker: Gelesia Adriano, lead peer educator of the Kiganamo group of women living with HIV
a1697.name: Gelesia Adriano
a1697.title: lead peer educator of the Kiganamo group of women living with HIV
a1697.speech: Said she was found to be HIV-positive in 2007; said that after tests showed she and her husband were infected, their youngest child, then 11 months old, was also found to be infected and died in 2011 because treatment was started too late; said that despite starting antiretroviral treatment in 2010 she lost hope after her husband died and stopped taking her medication because of loneliness, but that through the education she received after joining the Kiganamo group she regained hope and courage and now lives happily with another husband, with three children born while she was living with HIV who are not infected: "I welcome others to join the group; we share education on how to protect a child from infection. It has also helped us rise economically through members who have different incomes; we do entrepreneurship such as vegetable gardening and we guide each other about life."

a1697.speaker: Naomi Petro, woman living with HIV for nine years, Kiganamo group member
a1697.name: Naomi Petro
a1697.title: woman living with HIV for nine years, Kiganamo group member
a1697.speech: Urged women who are found to be infected not to live in fear but instead to be confident and close to the community around them by taking part in productive activities: "I came to be tested and was found to be infected in 2016, but I did not lose hope and to date I have four children, two of whom I bore when I already had the infection, but they do not have it because I follow the guidelines" ; said she sees no reason to live in fear and stress after joining the Kiganamo education group, which has helped her live a normal life without fear and be free to take part in social activities.

a1697.speaker: Consolata Amos, woman living with HIV, Kiganamo group member
a1697.name: Consolata Amos
a1697.title: woman living with HIV, Kiganamo group member
a1697.speech: Said that since she was found to have HIV in 2007 she has been living happily, contrary to what others think, and called on women not to despair when they are found to have HIV; explained that she lives a peaceful life, now lives with a husband with whom she started married life, and they have two children, both free of infection as a result of preventive education.

a1697.speaker: Dr Moshi Kigwinya, Kasulu District HIV Coordinator and Medical Officer in Charge of Kiganamo Health Centre
a1697.name: Dr Moshi Kigwinya
a1697.title: Kasulu District HIV Coordinator and Medical Officer in Charge of Kiganamo Health Centre
a1697.speech: Explained that mother-to-child transmission has declined through the group; said the group has made follow-up easier for those with new infections and has made Kasulu District the first in Kigoma Region in performing well in controlling mother-to-child HIV transmission; added that as a result of these successes infections in the district have fallen from 1.8 percent to 1.0 percent.

a1697.speaker: Geofrey Tarimo, Kigoma Region supervisor of Tanzania Health Program Supporters (THPS)
a1697.name: Geofrey Tarimo
a1697.title: Kigoma Region supervisor of Tanzania Health Program Supporters (THPS)
a1697.speech: Explained that through the existing cooperation between the government and private institutions, the implementation of health interventions, including the control of mother-to-child transmission, has succeeded; said that under the Afya Hatua project the organisation has funded motorcycles, vehicles and health professionals in order to reach people living in rural areas through the groups known as Psycho-Socio Support Groups (PSG); said the government, in cooperation with THPS and with funding from the United States Government through PEPFAR and CDC, has been implementing the Afya Hatua project at 74 facilities in the region's councils with the aim of controlling and reducing HIV infections.

a1697.speaker: Tanzania HIV Impact Survey (THIS) 2023/2024 (cited by Geofrey Tarimo)
a1697.name: Tanzania HIV Impact Survey (THIS) 2023/2024 (cited by Geofrey Tarimo)
a1697.speech: "According to statistics released in 2023/2024 by the Tanzania HIV Impact Survey (THIS), this region has 1.7 percent and is the region with the lowest infections in mainland Tanzania," he said.

a1788.speaker: Rwanda-DRC peace agreement (document, copy seen by Reuters)
a1788.name: Rwanda-DRC peace agreement (document
a1788.title: copy seen by Reuters)
a1788.speech: The agreement pledges to implement a 2024 deal that would see Rwandan troops withdraw from eastern Congo within 90 days ; says Kinshasa and Kigali will also launch a regional economic integration framework within 90 days ; gives Congo and Rwanda three months to launch a framework "to expand foreign trade and investment derived from regional critical mineral supply chains" ; voiced "full support" for the Qatar-hosted talks ; says Congo and Rwanda will form a joint security coordination mechanism within 30 days and implement a plan agreed last year to monitor and verify the withdrawal of Rwandan soldiers within three months ; says Rwanda and Congo will de-risk mineral supply chains and establish value chains "that link both countries, in partnership, as appropriate, with the U.S. and U.S. investors."

a1788.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a1788.name: Donald Trump
a1788.title: U.S. President
a1788.speech: "They were going at it for many years, and with machetes – it is one of the worst, one of the worst wars that anyone has ever seen. And I just happened to have somebody that was able to get it settled" ; "We're getting, for the United States, a lot of the mineral rights from the Congo as part of it. They're so honored to be here. They never thought they'd be coming."

a1788.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a1788.name: Donald Trump
a1788.title: U.S. President
a1788.speech: Warned of "very severe penalties, financial and otherwise", if the agreement is violated.

a1788.speaker: Olivier Nduhungirehe, Rwandan Foreign Minister
a1788.name: Olivier Nduhungirehe
a1788.title: Rwandan Foreign Minister
a1788.speech: Called the agreement a turning point ; told Trump that past deals had not been implemented and urged Trump to stay engaged.

a1788.speaker: Therese Kayikwamba Wagner, Congo Foreign Minister
a1788.name: Therese Kayikwamba Wagner
a1788.title: Congo Foreign Minister
a1788.speech: Said it must be followed by disengagement.

a1788.speaker: Massad Boulos, Trump's senior adviser for Africa
a1788.name: Massad Boulos
a1788.title: Trump's senior adviser for Africa
a1788.speech: Dubbed the package of agreements the "Washington Accord" ; told Reuters in May that Washington wanted the peace agreement and accompanying minerals deals to be signed simultaneously this summer.

a1788.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a1788.name: Marco Rubio
a1788.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a1788.speech: Said on Friday that heads of state would be "here in Washington in a few weeks to finalize the complete protocol and agreement."

a1788.speaker: Source familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1788.name: Source familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1788.speech: Told Reuters on Friday that another agreement on the framework would be signed by the heads of state at a separate White House event at an unspecified time ; said there is an understanding that progress in ongoing talks in Doha – a separate but parallel mediation effort with delegations from the Congolese government and M23 – is essential before the signing of the economic framework.

a1788.speaker: Analysts and diplomats
a1788.name: Analysts and diplomats
a1788.speech: According to analysts and diplomats, Rwanda has sent at least 7,000 soldiers over the border in support of the M23 rebels.

a1788.speaker: Reuters (report)
a1788.name: Reuters (report)
a1788.speech: Reported on Thursday that Congolese negotiators had dropped an earlier demand that Rwandan troops immediately leave eastern Congo, paving the way for the signing ceremony on Friday.

a1788.speaker: Congo, the United Nations and Western powers
a1788.name: Congo
a1788.title: the United Nations and Western powers
a1788.speech: Say Rwanda is supporting M23 by sending troops and arms.

a1788.speaker: Rwanda (government position)
a1788.name: Rwanda (government position)
a1788.speech: Has long denied helping M23, saying its forces are acting in self-defence against Congo's army and ethnic Hutu militiamen linked to the 1994 Rwandan genocide, including the FDLR.

a1788.speaker: Jason Stearns, political scientist at Simon Fraser University in Canada specialising in Africa's Great Lakes region
a1788.name: Jason Stearns
a1788.title: political scientist at Simon Fraser University in Canada specialising in Africa's Great Lakes region
a1788.speech: "This is the best chance we have at a peace process for the moment despite all the challenges and flaws" ; added that similar formulas have been attempted before, and "it will be up to the U.S., as they are the godfather of this deal, to make sure both sides abide by the terms."

a1788.speaker: Tresor Kibangula, political analyst at Congo's Ebuteli research institute
a1788.name: Tresor Kibangula
a1788.title: political analyst at Congo's Ebuteli research institute
a1788.speech: Said the terms carry "a strategic message: securing the east also means securing investments" ; added "It remains to be seen whether this economic logic will suffice" to end the fighting.

a1861.speaker: Officials at the US Embassy in Lilongwe
a1861.name: Officials at the US Embassy in Lilongwe
a1861.speech: Said in a written response yesterday that they needed more time before responding to our questionnaire.

a1861.speaker: Marcus Muhariwa, US Embassy strategic communications specialist
a1861.name: Marcus Muhariwa
a1861.title: US Embassy strategic communications specialist
a1861.speech: "Looking at how complex the issues raised are, we will not be able to respond to meet your deadline."

a1861.speaker: Nancy Tembo, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malawi (non-response)
a1861.name: Nancy Tembo
a1861.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malawi (non-response)
a1861.speech: Had not yet responded to our questionnaire by press time at 9pm yesterday.

a1861.speaker: Williams Banda, Treasury spokesperson
a1861.name: Williams Banda
a1861.title: Treasury spokesperson
a1861.speech: Said they have yet to inform Foreign Affairs officials on the implications of the executive orders.

a1861.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1861.name: Donald Trump
a1861.title: US President
a1861.speech: Said during the announcement on Monday that according to US policy, no further foreign assistance shall be disbursed in ways that are contrary to their foreign policy: "All department and agency heads with responsibility for United States foreign development assistance programs shall immediately pause new obligations and disbursements of development assistance funds to foreign countries and implement non-governmental organisations, international organisations, and contractors pending reviews." ; further said department and agency heads, with assistance from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), will decide on whether to continue, modify, or stop foreign assistance, where the Secretary of State and OMB director will play crucial roles in approving modified obligations for programmes.

a1861.speaker: Milward Tobias, economist
a1861.name: Milward Tobias
a1861.title: economist
a1861.speech: Said in an interview yesterday that at this point it remains unclear if Malawi will be within the US government's priority areas at the end of the 90-day review window: "Aid for programmes comes through different channels, local and international organisations. We do not know if funding for programmes will continue within and after the 90 days."

a1861.speaker: Bertha Bangara-Chikadza, acting president of the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a1861.name: Bertha Bangara-Chikadza
a1861.title: acting president of the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a1861.speech: Said US-funded programmes whose funding was already disbursed, like the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Compact, are unlikely to be affected.

a1861.speaker: USAid website
a1861.name: USAid website
a1861.speech: According to the USAid website, the US government has invested more than $196 million (about K343 billion) to implement the National Reading Programme in all of Malawi's public primary schools.

a1990.speaker: US Mission in Nigeria (security alert statement)
a1990.name: US Mission in Nigeria (security alert statement)
a1990.speech: issued a security alert to Americans in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja: “Due to increased security concerns arising from current global developments, US Mission Nigeria informs US citizens that all US Embassy employees and their families are prohibited from non-official travel to a Nigerian military site or other government venue in Abuja at this time.” ; “Actions to take: Stay alert in public places, with particular attention to locations and venues where Westerners, expatriates, and government officials frequent. Avoid large gatherings and consider limiting unnecessary travel. Avoid predictable routines. Familiarise yourself with emergency exits when you enter buildings. Review your personal security plans.” ; “The Consular Sections of Embassy Abuja and Consulate General Lagos remain open.”

a1990.speaker: US Consulate in Nigeria
a1990.name: US Consulate in Nigeria
a1990.speech: advised American citizens to avoid non-essential travel to military and government facilities in Abuja, citing increased global security concerns.

a1990.speaker: US Embassy in Abuja
a1990.name: US Embassy in Abuja
a1990.speech: announced that all embassy staff and their families are now barred from visiting military sites or other government venues in the Nigerian capital unless required for official duties.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique, chaired by President Patrice Talon)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique
a2120.title: chaired by President Patrice Talon)
a2120.speech: Adopted decrees on the creation, organisation, composition and functioning of the regional Millennium Challenge Account-Benin; on the application of law no. 2017-29 of 15 March 2018 on radiological safety and nuclear security in the Republic of Benin; and on the approval of the statutes of the Beninese Company for Digital Infrastructure (Sbin) S.a.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.speech: Authorised the organisation of a recruitment competition in 2023 for 15 auditors at the General Inspectorate of Finance and instructed the ministers concerned to ensure its proper conduct, noting that retirements from 2027 would create a shortage of qualified personnel.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.speech: Gave its agreement for the contractual formalities with the selected company for the construction of the stormwater collector and the development of the access roads to the referral hospital at Abomey-Calavi, ahead of the infrastructure's entry into service during 2024.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.speech: Authorised contracting with various service providers for the emergency development works in the southern zone of the Esplanade des Amazones for the 50th edition of the petanque world championships, and instructed the ministers in charge to ensure the works are conducted according to the required standards and deadlines.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.speech: Decided on the construction of an 18-hole championship Golf course at Avlekete in the commune of Ouidah, saying it appeared opportune to include Golf as a sporting discipline to strengthen the attractiveness of the site and encourage the organisation of competitions in Benin, with the various components entrusted to internationally renowned providers.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.speech: Said the Government plans to have a sector plan drawn up for the area of influence of the Glo-Djigbe Special Economic Zone, with the prospect of nearly 300,000 jobs by 2030, to organise land use over a fifteen-year horizon and avoid disorderly development; the minister in charge of the Living Environment will undertake the steps for contracting with the identified groupings.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.speech: Agreed to the reinforcement works and the acquisition of complementary equipment at the Save hospital, whose completion rate is close to 90% and where care has been provided since December 2022.

a2120.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a2120.speech: Announced Benin's participation in the 40th session of the Council of Ministers of the African and Malagasy Council for Higher Education (Cames), from 23 to 27 May 2023 in Niamey, Niger, and in the 111th session of the International Labour Conference and other meetings from 5 to 16 June 2023 in Geneva, Switzerland; and announced the appointment of Mr Olatoundji Martin Essoun as Deputy Director of Planning, Administration and Finance at the ministry of Nursery and Primary Education.

a2120.speaker: Edouard Ouin-Ouro, Secretary General of the Government of Benin
a2120.name: Edouard Ouin-Ouro
a2120.title: Secretary General of the Government of Benin
a2120.speech: Signed and issued the communique of the council of ministers, done at Cotonou on 24 May 2023.

a2218.speaker: King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, President of the Council of Ministers
a2218.name: King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud
a2218.title: Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, President of the Council of Ministers
a2218.speech: Ordered KSrelief to provide $100 million in humanitarian aid and to organise a national fundraising campaign through the "Sahem" platform for the Sudanese people, to alleviate the hardships they face.

a2218.speaker: Dr. Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al-Rabeeah, Adviser to the Royal Court and Supervisor General of KSrelief
a2218.name: Dr. Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al-Rabeeah
a2218.title: Adviser to the Royal Court and Supervisor General of KSrelief
a2218.speech: Affirmed that the assistance stems from the will of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques and of HRH the Crown Prince to stand alongside the Sudanese people and to mitigate the impact of the crisis in Sudan.

a2218.speaker: Dr. Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al-Rabeeah, Adviser to the Royal Court and Supervisor General of KSrelief
a2218.name: Dr. Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al-Rabeeah
a2218.title: Adviser to the Royal Court and Supervisor General of KSrelief
a2218.speech: Expressed his sincere gratitude to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques and to HRH the Crown Prince for their noble positions, which are a continuation of the humanitarian role of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in standing alongside disaster-stricken and needy people everywhere in the world, and revealed that under the generous directives, relief goods and humanitarian and medical aid would be provided to displaced people in the Republic of Sudan.

a2396.speaker: Ethiopian government
a2396.name: Ethiopian government
a2396.speech: Announces the final phase of its offensive in Tigray.

a2396.speaker: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2396.name: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2396.speech: Has prepared a response plan intended to help two million individuals in the Tigray, Afar and Amhara regions; the projection includes aid currently being provided and also takes into account an additional 1.1 million people who would need assistance as a result of the conflict. About 76 million dollars are needed to fund the plan.

a2478.speaker: Union of Industry, Agriculture, Commerce and Related Services (SIACSA)
a2478.name: Union of Industry
a2478.title: Agriculture, Commerce and Related Services (SIACSA)
a2478.speech: Denounced today the job insecurity of the new prison officers and their families, criticising the delay by the Ministry of Justice in the definitive appointment of the 99 trained professionals; the union also announced a strike and a simultaneous demonstration for 17 March as a form of protest against the situation, and wants a response from the Ministry of Justice on the labour situation of the new prison officers.

a2591.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.name: Russell Dlamini
a2591.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.speech: Expressed his pleasure in receiving the new U.S. Chargé d’Affaires Marc Weinstock, describing him as a person who “radiates a pleasant personality and vibrant energy.”

a2591.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.name: Russell Dlamini
a2591.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.speech: Acknowledged the commendable work of Weinstock’s predecessor, Caitlin Piper, noting that she “worked well with the current Administration of the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini and successfully strengthened the relations between the two countries”, and wished Piper success in her new assignment.

a2591.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.name: Russell Dlamini
a2591.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.speech: Emphasised that their discussions focused on “the opportunities that we can seize working together to serve our countries as well as to further strengthen our relations”, identifying food security, border surveillance, and disaster risk management as key areas for collaboration.

a2591.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.name: Russell Dlamini
a2591.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
