a2591.speech: Touched on the recent reinstatement of critical health programs funded by USAID and PEPFAR, which are vital for HIV/AIDS prevention, care, and treatment in Eswatini, highlighting the importance of these programs in safeguarding public health and noting the arrival of third-country migrants from the U.S.

a2591.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.name: Russell Dlamini
a2591.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a2591.speech: Described the United States as “one of the country’s most valuable diplomatic partners” and underscored that the relationship is “based on mutual trust and respect for one another”, reaffirming Eswatini’s commitment to fostering deeper cooperation; “To you, Chargé d’Affaires, seize the opportunity because time and chance have happened. Welcome to the Kingdom of Eswatini, the palace of Africa.”

a2597.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.name: Mohammed Ali
a2597.title: Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.speech: Explained on OK FM’s afternoon show that if people paid for the service, much work would be done and more people would have access to water compared to the low percentage currently recorded by the company: “We have begun a massive disconnection exercise. We started off today (Monday February 11, 2024) around the Duport area and that will continue until we can collect more than 50 percent of our debt. Just for this year, from January to October, there is uncollected debt of nearly one million United States Dollars. We have 14,000 customers but less than 5,000 of this number pay bills” ; noted that the failure on the part of the majority of the customers to pay bills continues to deny the company sufficient funds to underwrite costs for maintenance, extension of service to communities yet to have access, as well as providing security and other services.

a2597.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.name: Mohammed Ali
a2597.title: Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.speech: “We do not have the money to pay for the extension of the main pipe into the communities. We understand that access to water is a fundamental human right but in order to continue having it, it is good that people pay. Water bills are not that high. An average home uses less than 5,000 gallons per month and it costs around US$10. A single individual using water pays US$5 or even less than, depending on the usage” ; “There are some communities that are just using water without paying and when there is no water supply they can be the loudest in criticizing” ; admonished all interested in having and using water to visit the company’s website, download a form, register and proceed to its office for connection after paying about US$200, and appealed to all to pay for water and connect legally.

a2597.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.name: Mohammed Ali
a2597.title: Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.speech: Noted that the construction of a dosing unit to effectuate the application of chlorine into the water for its purification has been completed, and said powder chlorine is being used instead of liquid chlorine due to the many security conditions associated with its importation: “The chlorine dosing unit will transform the powder into a liquid form and it will be used into the clear water wells. The dozing chlorine unit will determine the exact quantity of chlorine that is required to disinfect any given quantity of water, even millions of gallons.”

a2597.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.name: Mohammed Ali
a2597.title: Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.speech: “The second development is that we now have a booster station at Caldwell Junction. It got burned in 2021. The water is pumped from the treatment plant in Caldwell and before it reaches Duala, the pressure drops. If functioning, it helps to pump water all the way to St. Paul Bridge and also towards town” ; explained that since the booster got burned, residents in Duala and central Monrovia have not been receiving water but the problem has been resolved and the dedication of the facility will take place before this month; “We have just completed that and are now installing the electrical facilities.” He put the cost for the booster construction at US$136,000 while the chlorine unit costs US$82,000.

a2597.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.name: Mohammed Ali
a2597.title: Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a2597.speech: “We just signed a contract for the construction of a water supply system in Bopolu City. It is the same thing we have in Kakata and Robertsport. We will run pipes to government offices and hospitals and some other buildings. When people want water they can pay for connection to their homes. That is expected to be completed in February” ; named Greenville in Sinoe, Pleebo in Maryland and subsequently Zwedru in Grand Gedeh County as cities that will benefit from the first plan which is expected to run up to 2026; disclosed that the sum of US$60,000 has been secured through the Ministry of Finance to conduct a feasibility study in the counties.

a2654.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM), UN agency (statement)
a2654.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a2654.title: UN agency (statement)
a2654.speech: The WFP trucks were carrying “essential food supplies for starving populations, who were anxiously awaiting aid”, the UN agency said in a statement, adding that “hunger, desperation and anxiety about the arrival of aid are increasing insecurity” in the Gaza Strip.

a2654.speaker: Israeli Government (announcement)
a2654.name: Israeli Government (announcement)
a2654.speech: Announced today that it had allowed 107 trucks from the UN and the international community to enter the Gaza Strip on Thursday.

a2654.speaker: United Nations
a2654.name: United Nations
a2654.speech: On that day, the UN said that 198 trucks entered Gaza, 90 of which were distributed across the enclave, and that most were loaded with medical supplies or flour for the small territory’s bakeries.

a2654.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM), UN agency
a2654.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a2654.title: UN agency
a2654.speech: The WFP declared today that it cannot “operate safely in a distribution system that limits the number of bakeries and locations where people in Gaza can access food”. ; “We need the support of the Israeli authorities to deliver much larger volumes of food aid to Gaza more quickly, consistently and through safer routes, as was done during the ceasefire,” argued the UN agency, which wants to be able to deliver flour and food parcels directly to families, since it considers this “the most effective way to combat widespread hunger”. ; Two million people in the Gaza Strip face extreme hunger if immediate measures are not taken, the UN programme warned.

a2654.speaker: Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for UN Secretary-General António Guterres
a2654.name: Stéphane Dujarric
a2654.title: spokesperson for UN Secretary-General António Guterres
a2654.speech: Said on Thursday that the humanitarian aid allowed by Israel into Gaza in recent days “does not even come close to covering the scale and volume of the needs of Gaza’s 2.1 million inhabitants”.

a2828.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.name: Mohamed Guirreh Galab
a2828.title: president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.speech: “The objective of this training is to create innovative social enterprises with positive impacts in our community” ; said the training week is entitled GO, to welcome the participants of the first phase, Know, and that it was six days of training on putting together their business model dossier.

a2828.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.name: Mohamed Guirreh Galab
a2828.title: president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.speech: On the objective of the training, said it was first necessary to clarify the semantics of social entrepreneurship, recalling that Cantillon, a forerunner of the theory of entrepreneurship, affirmed in 1755 that the entrepreneur is an important actor who influences the economic market, and that Schumpeter defined, in 1911, the entrepreneur as a person who innovates and creates new combinations, new products or new processes; said that today both researchers and economists consider entrepreneurial activity to be essential to a country's economic vigour, that social entrepreneurship is the action deployed by an entrepreneur to find innovative solutions to social problems, and that “the objective pursued is to support project holders in order to create social enterprises with a positive impact in Djibouti.”

a2828.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.name: Mohamed Guirreh Galab
a2828.title: president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.speech: On difficulties encountered, said: “The main challenge was to gather fifty entrepreneurs and project holders coming from all six regions of our national territory in one and the same place, ‘Sunny Hill’. It was a first, in order to develop the entrepreneurial spirit, create a network and a favourable environment outside their comfort zone.”

a2828.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.name: Mohamed Guirreh Galab
a2828.title: president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
a2828.speech: Said the participants had very interesting ideas in different sectors such as agriculture, fishing, industry or training.

a2928.speaker: African Union officials
a2928.name: African Union officials
a2928.speech: Questioned how Africa could deepen trade ties with the United States under what they called “abusive” tariff proposals and tightening visa conditions largely targeting travellers from Africa.

a2928.speaker: Ambassador Troy Fitrell, top U.S. diplomat for Africa
a2928.name: Ambassador Troy Fitrell
a2928.title: top U.S. diplomat for Africa
a2928.speech: Dismissed allegations of unfair U.S. trade practices; “There is no visitation ban,” he said during a press conference at the U.S.-Africa Business Summit in Luanda, and said that U.S. consulates continue issuing visas regularly, although some now come with shorter validity periods due to concerns over overstays.

a2928.speaker: Ambassador Troy Fitrell, top U.S. diplomat for Africa
a2928.name: Ambassador Troy Fitrell
a2928.title: top U.S. diplomat for Africa
a2928.speech: Said that the proposed U.S. import tariffs were not yet implemented, and negotiations were ongoing to create a more reciprocal trading environment, including through the renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA).

a2928.speaker: Ambassador Troy Fitrell, top U.S. diplomat for Africa
a2928.name: Ambassador Troy Fitrell
a2928.title: top U.S. diplomat for Africa
a2928.speech: Said that funding delays would not derail the Lobito Corridor railway project connecting Angola, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo, and reaffirmed his country’s commitment to it: “It’s not at risk,” he said of the initiative, describing it as a “win-win” for U.S. investors and African economies, and underscoring its significance for regional integration.

a2928.speaker: Several African business and political leaders
a2928.name: Several African business and political leaders
a2928.speech: Have raised concerns about a sharp drop in visa approvals, particularly for travellers from West Africa, since late 2023.

a2928.speaker: Lesotho and Madagascar (African economies)
a2928.name: Lesotho and Madagascar (African economies)
a2928.speech: Warned that even a baseline 10% levy could threaten critical exports such as apparel and minerals.

a2928.speaker: Angolan President João Lourenço
a2928.name: Angolan President João Lourenço
a2928.speech: Addressing more than 2,000 government and business leaders at the summit, said U.S. companies should shift from aid to investment-driven partnerships: “It is time to replace the logic of aid with the logic of investment and trade,” urging diversification into sectors such as automotive manufacturing, shipbuilding, tourism, cement, and steel production.

a2928.speaker: Bureau of African Affairs (@AsstSecStateAF), social media posts
a2928.name: Bureau of African Affairs (@AsstSecStateAF)
a2928.title: social media posts
a2928.speech: “Senior Bureau Official Troy Fitrell thanked Angola President João Lourenço for hosting the 2025 @CorpCnclAfrica U.S.-Africa Business Summit and for Angola’s commitment to building economic partnerships with the United States and across the continent.” ; “After three days, the @CorpCnclAfrica #USAfricaBizSummit was a success. We launched new deals between U.S. companies and African entities and strengthened relationships between the U.S. and African governments. Our relationships aren’t all about business though! SBO Fitrell…”

a2928.speaker: U.S. Senior Advisor for Africa (@US_SrAdvisorAF), social media post
a2928.name: U.S. Senior Advisor for Africa (@US_SrAdvisorAF)
a2928.title: social media post
a2928.speech: “At the @CorpCnclAfrica U.S.-Africa Business Summit in Angola, I spoke about the importance of the U.S.-Africa economic partnership. The Trump administration is focused on supporting peace in Africa because we recognize the critical link between peace, stability, and economic…”

a3032.speaker: Nicolau dos Santos, Chairman of the Board of RTP (Radio e Televisão Portuguesa)
a3032.name: Nicolau dos Santos
a3032.title: Chairman of the Board of RTP (Radio e Televisão Portuguesa)
a3032.speech: Opened up opportunities for internships and technical and professional training for TVM workers ; gave guarantees to his TVM counterpart about the possibility of sending TVM technicians for internships and professional training activities at RTP.

a3032.speaker: Victor Nhatitima, Chairman of the Board of TVM (Televisão de Moçambique)
a3032.name: Victor Nhatitima
a3032.title: Chairman of the Board of TVM (Televisão de Moçambique)
a3032.speech: Is seeking support in technologies, knowledge and other opportunities for strengthening institutional capacity for the repositioning of TVM in the market.

a3032.speaker: Mozambican Football Federation
a3032.name: Mozambican Football Federation
a3032.speech: Guarantees that it is working, at all costs, for the best of the national team, two days before the end of the contract of national coach Chiquinho Conde; the position was taken on Thursday during a meeting held with the Ministry of Youth and Sports, Caifadine Manasse.

a3032.speaker: Francisco Pagula, Governor of Inhambane
a3032.name: Francisco Pagula
a3032.title: Governor of Inhambane
a3032.speech: Advocates the consolidation of the cultural and creative industry as one of the main drivers for boosting tourism and local economic development, speaking on Thursday during the reception for the runner-up of the international competition “Miss World Culture 2025” held in Nigeria.

a3032.speaker: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3032.name: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3032.speech: Said in the speech relaunching the TotalEnergies liquefied natural gas project on the Afungi Peninsula that the act represents Mozambique's capacity to overcome challenges and recover the confidence of international investors.

a3032.speaker: Gueta Chapo, First Lady of Mozambique
a3032.name: Gueta Chapo
a3032.title: First Lady of Mozambique
a3032.speech: Appeals for the unity of Mozambicans in order to respond to the needs of the families affected by the floods, saying that strengthening cooperation is fundamental in order to save lives and restore dignity to the victims of disasters.

a3032.speaker: Spokesperson of the PRM (Mozambique Republic Police)
a3032.name: Spokesperson of the PRM (Mozambique Republic Police)
a3032.speech: Said the collapse of an illegal mine that killed five artisanal miners and injured five others in the locality of Movinha, Gurúè District, Zambézia Province, happened last Monday.

a3032.speaker: Chief Executive of TotalEnergies
a3032.name: Chief Executive of TotalEnergies
a3032.speech: Announces a donation of 200 million meticais in support of the victims of the floods in the south and centre of the country.

a3093.speaker: Stakeholders in Nigeria's health sector
a3093.name: Stakeholders in Nigeria's health sector
a3093.speech: Have raised concern over the reduction in donor and partner funding for immunisation programmes, warning that the country risks a public health crisis if sustainable alternatives are not put in place; they emphasised the need for continued commitment and strategic planning to ensure long-term vaccine availability and coverage.

a3093.speaker: Chika Offor, Chief Executive Officer of the Vaccine Network for Disease Control (VNDC)
a3093.name: Chika Offor
a3093.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Vaccine Network for Disease Control (VNDC)
a3093.speech: Said the decline in international support, including from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), is already affecting Nigeria's immunisation efforts; noted that vaccines play a key role in saving lives and reducing healthcare costs; explained that the 2025 budget included N231.7 billion for immunisation, malaria vaccination, and vaccine tracking, calling it "a significant milestone toward universal vaccine coverage"; said with the exit of USAID funding and diminishing donor support, Nigeria's vaccine financing is more vulnerable than ever ; "Shrinking fiscal space and competing national priorities further threaten immunisation programmes. If we do not act swiftly, we risk reversing the progress made in 2024."

a3093.speaker: Ibrahim Oloriegbe, Chairman of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3093.name: Ibrahim Oloriegbe
a3093.title: Chairman of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3093.speech: Emphasised the importance of consistent vaccine financing; highlighted the complexity of the vaccine supply chain—from national procurement and donor involvement to state distribution and local delivery—and stressed the critical role of the cold chain infrastructure ; "The cold chain is a critical part of that entire chain. Without proper storage and temperature control, vaccines lose their efficacy" ; while acknowledging the expected roles of state and local governments in vaccine delivery, he noted persistent gaps, adding that this is where civil society and partners step in.

a3093.speaker: Mohammed Usman, former House of Representatives member
a3093.name: Mohammed Usman
a3093.title: former House of Representatives member
a3093.speech: Expressed deep frustration over delayed vaccine financing, saying the amount budgeted for vaccines in the 2024 budget is yet to be released ; "That is very sad" ; urged President Bola Tinubu to demonstrate leadership by ensuring prompt disbursement of funds ; "The President must lead by example," adding that Health Minister Muhammad Pate is well-positioned to drive the reforms needed; called for stronger local government participation ; "Every level—federal, state, and local—has its role to play. And local governments must also show that they are ready to fulfil their responsibilities."

a3093.speaker: Mohammed Usman, former House of Representatives member
a3093.name: Mohammed Usman
a3093.title: former House of Representatives member
a3093.speech: Urged the government to restore Nigeria's capacity to produce vaccines locally, recalling that the country had such capabilities in the 1970s, and explained that if Nigeria had sustained that effort, the country wouldn't be talking about dependency today but would be exporting to other African countries ; "What is 10 billion compared to what Nigerians spend on things of no real value? We need 50 to 100 billion for vaccine production. Without it, we'll remain dependent."

a3093.speaker: State of Health of the Nation report
a3093.name: State of Health of the Nation report
a3093.speech: The latest State of Health of the Nation report highlighted the need to strengthen local manufacturing of medicines and vaccines to sustain the current push for local vaccine production through policy incentives and increased private sector investment.

a3093.speaker: Oyeyemi Pitan, Executive Director of Gem Hub Initiative and co-convener of the Joint Learning Agenda for UHC in Nigeria
a3093.name: Oyeyemi Pitan
a3093.title: Executive Director of Gem Hub Initiative and co-convener of the Joint Learning Agenda for UHC in Nigeria
a3093.speech: Commended the collective efforts of stakeholders in prioritising the health of Nigerian children through stronger immunisation systems; underscored the importance of ensuring that every child, especially those in underserved and remote communities, is reached with essential vaccines; noted that partners are working through the Sustainable Development Goal 3 Global Action Plan (SDG3 GAP) and are collaborating with the Nigerian government to identify and immunise zero-dose children while also reinforcing national immunisation structures.

a3135.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a3135.name: Boni Yayi
a3135.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a3135.speech: “God is a democrat, which is why democracy is non-negotiable. For us, the world can only move towards democracy in order to solve its problems” ; affirms Benin’s commitment to strengthening its democracy, holding that Benin’s 25-year-old democracy is an irreversible process, all the more so because his country shares the values of the free world.

a3135.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a3135.name: Boni Yayi
a3135.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a3135.speech: Maintains that this democracy needs to be supported by strong institutions that work for the general interest: “One cannot conceive of a democracy without the rule of law, and there is no rule of law without a functioning justice system. Without justice, impunity and corruption cannot be fought. We must make progress in the area of sanctions, otherwise we will not be able to attract investors” ; continues that Benin defends freedom of expression through the flourishing of the media, which deserve to be reformed for a more solid democratic anchoring ; also defends the freedom of the population to move about in production areas, which presupposes the need to guarantee their security by investing more in the fight against terrorism.

a3135.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a3135.name: Boni Yayi
a3135.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a3135.speech: Welcomes the signing of the second MCA compact: “Energy will make it possible to create economies of scale in order to promote self-employment and move towards strong growth” ; taking stock of the first MCA compact, considers that the programme genuinely brought added value to Benin’s economy, notably through improved performance of the port of Cotonou and the modernisation of the justice system, financial services and land administration, while acknowledging that Benin stumbled in the fight against corruption, which explains the delay in obtaining eligibility for the second compact ; “The MCA is a tool that responds to the economic and social transformation needs of our country. Today we are ready to erase our shortcomings in order to carry out the second-generation MCA successfully” ; considers that the first generation of MCA already contains elements of integration, inasmuch as the investments made had a knock-on effect on the whole sub-region.

a3135.speaker: Dana Hyde, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3135.name: Dana Hyde
a3135.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3135.speech: Argues that investment in the energy sector is today an imperative for Benin; recalls that only a third of the country’s population has electricity, and those who do have it do not have it full time: “The compact uses a comprehensive approach to develop a sustainable energy sector for Benin” ; explains that eligibility for the MCA rests on a rigorous selection process based on indicators relating to economic freedom, governance, and the country’s level of investment in its people, and that Benin’s new eligibility, following Ghana and Cape Verde, constitutes a performance indicator to be welcomed.

a3135.speaker: Dana Hyde, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3135.name: Dana Hyde
a3135.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3135.speech: Also supports the need for African countries to invest more in integrating their economies, noting that the MCA programme envisages setting up regional compacts in the coming years: “We are optimistic that we can do it.”

a3156.speaker: Inhlase (2024) report
a3156.name: Inhlase (2024) report
a3156.speech: Cited as showing that the ACC faces chronic underfunding and capacity shortages limiting the commission’s capacity to investigate cases, train staff and conduct public education.

a3156.speaker: Eswatini Observer (2025)
a3156.name: Eswatini Observer (2025)
a3156.speech: Revealed that the absence of whistle-blower laws discourages insiders from reporting corruption.

a3156.speaker: Afrobarometer survey of 2023
a3156.name: Afrobarometer survey of 2023
a3156.speech: Revealed that a majority of emaSwati found corruption to be worsening and that reporting could invite retaliation.

a3156.speaker: IMF (2023) report
a3156.name: IMF (2023) report
a3156.speech: Cited as showing that prosecution outcomes remain weak, with only 2 of 258 investigated cases referred for prosecution in one year.

a3156.speaker: IMF (2023) report
a3156.name: IMF (2023) report
a3156.speech: Cited for the finding that a key priority is building greater financial and human resource capacity through increased and ring-fenced funding, coupled with professional training in areas such as forensic auditing, digital investigation and case management, which would significantly enhance the ACC’s investigative capabilities.

a3156.speaker: Africa Press (2023)
a3156.name: Africa Press (2023)
a3156.speech: Cited for the finding that addressing internal corruption and ensuring merit-based recruitment is crucial to restoring credibility and public confidence.

a3156.speaker: Afrobarometer (2023)
a3156.name: Afrobarometer (2023)
a3156.speech: Cited for the recommendation of enhancing the commission’s institutional independence by restructuring its reporting lines, so that it reports directly to Parliament rather than the Ministry of Justice, thereby minimising political interference in its operations.

a3156.speaker: Inhlase (2024) report
a3156.name: Inhlase (2024) report
a3156.speech: Cited for the recommendation that the ACC must focus on building public trust and engagement through robust public education campaigns, improved transparency in case handling and closer collaboration with civil society organisations to foster a culture of accountability and collective responsibility in the fight against corruption.

a3188.speaker: Foreign Minister of Niger
a3188.name: Foreign Minister of Niger
a3188.speech: "We are ready to invite more Russian instructors."

a3188.speaker: Sergei Lavrov, Russian Foreign Minister
a3188.name: Sergei Lavrov
a3188.title: Russian Foreign Minister
a3188.speech: Said the president of Burkina Faso is coming to Moscow to celebrate Victory Day.

a3188.speaker: Sergei Lavrov, Russian Foreign Minister
a3188.name: Sergei Lavrov
a3188.title: Russian Foreign Minister
a3188.speech: Said trade between Russia and the AES (Alliance of Sahel States) countries has increased tenfold in one year.

a3188.speaker: Media reports
a3188.name: Media reports
a3188.speech: Reported that the president of Angola received an invitation from Putin to take part in the Victory Parade ; Reported that Al-Shabaab in Somalia fired mortar shells at the area of Mogadishu airport ; Reported that employees of the Romanian interior ministry worked as mercenaries in the DRC during their holidays.

a3188.speaker: Foreign Minister of Mali
a3188.name: Foreign Minister of Mali
a3188.speech: Said the president is visiting Russia in June.

a3188.speaker: Foreign Minister of Mali
a3188.name: Foreign Minister of Mali
a3188.speech: Called Ukraine a sponsor of terrorism.

a3188.speaker: AFP (Agence France-Presse)
a3188.name: AFP (Agence France-Presse)
a3188.speech: Reported that the authorities of the DRC are in secret negotiations with the M23 rebels in Qatar.

a3188.speaker: Rosoboronexport (Russian arms export agency)
a3188.name: Rosoboronexport (Russian arms export agency)
a3188.speech: Said it is ready to help the AES countries arm themselves to fight piracy.

a3188.speaker: Source (anonymous)
a3188.name: Source (anonymous)
a3188.speech: Said organizers of demonstrations in the Central African Republic attracted young people with free beer.

a3188.speaker: Foreign Minister of Niger
a3188.name: Foreign Minister of Niger
a3188.speech: Allowed for the possibility of building a nuclear power plant with the support of the Russian Federation.

a3188.speaker: President of Zimbabwe
a3188.name: President of Zimbabwe
a3188.speech: Declared the removal of duties on goods coming from the United States.

a3188.speaker: Rosatom
a3188.name: Rosatom
a3188.speech: Said the number of specialists for the construction of a nuclear power plant in Egypt will increase to 30,000.

a3188.speaker: Expert (unnamed)
a3188.name: Expert (unnamed)
a3188.speech: Stated what the foreign ministers of the Russian Federation and the Sahel countries will discuss ; Spoke about the goals of the Sahel countries in foreign policy.

a3338.speaker: Several truck drivers at the Jah Oil Cement depot in Brikama
a3338.name: Several truck drivers at the Jah Oil Cement depot in Brikama
a3338.speech: Described their situation as unbearable and frustrating; they had spent several days at the gate without receiving assistance or their supplies.

a3338.speaker: Amadou Bah, truck driver
a3338.name: Amadou Bah
a3338.title: truck driver
a3338.speech: Shared that he has been waiting in line for six days to load his cement supply but has yet to make any progress; mentioned that it could take him another day or two to enter the factory complex to load the cement; described the situation as frustrating and costly for himself and his two apprentices, noting that the longer he stayed, the more he had to pay for food, water, and other necessities.

a3338.speaker: Madi Barrow, truck driver
a3338.name: Madi Barrow
a3338.title: truck driver
a3338.speech: "Today is my fourth day here, and I cannot even enter the factory to get loaded. I cannot say when I will leave here. It may take me another two or three days before I get my turn to load" ; "I have never experienced such a delay at the factory. Usually, I get loaded the very day I come here. We are all very concerned and frustrated because of the long wait to get loaded, coupled with the extra spending."

a3338.speaker: Ahmat Kah, truck driver from Jambur
a3338.name: Ahmat Kah
a3338.title: truck driver from Jambur
a3338.speech: Informed TAT that he had spent three days at the cement factory, implying that this situation affects their business, families, and other needs; mentioned that factory officials informed him about issues with the production machine's conveyor belt, and that as a result production had significantly decreased, leading to a low supply.

a3338.speaker: Jah Oil factory officials (via truck driver Ahmat Kah)
a3338.name: Jah Oil factory officials (via truck driver Ahmat Kah)
a3338.speech: Informed him about issues with the production machine's conveyor belt, noting that as a result production had significantly decreased, leading to a low supply.

a3338.speaker: Alieu Jallow, truck driver
a3338.name: Alieu Jallow
a3338.title: truck driver
a3338.speech: Described the situation and feelings of other drivers, noting that the lengthy queue at the Jah Oil Cement factory is taking a toll on them; said this is compounded by the high food and water prices available at the factory site, and that some drivers have to pay fares to Brikama or Farato to buy food and drinking water, unbudgeted spending that most drivers need to be wary of before coming to the factory.

a3338.speaker: Anonymous cement dealer
a3338.name: Anonymous cement dealer
a3338.speech: Has blamed the Gambian Government for the current situation, stating that the government has created a monopoly in the cement business by limiting suppliers to just a few: "These suppliers are unable to meet the market's demand" ; also argued that cement packaging companies should be honest with the government and the public about their capacity to adequately supply the market ; "It's very unfortunate; truck drivers must wait days without getting cement at the factory. I challenge Jah Oil to come out and clear the air about why this situation happened."

a3338.speaker: CEO of Jah Oil Company
a3338.name: CEO of Jah Oil Company
a3338.speech: As we went to press, we were unsuccessful in speaking with the CEO of Jah Oil Company to clarify the development.

a3338.speaker: The Cement Importers and Traders Alliance of The Gambia
a3338.name: The Cement Importers and Traders Alliance of The Gambia
a3338.speech: Has alleged that local cement bagging companies are underfilling their bags and selling them as 50 kg to consumers, including Jah Oil; the members alleged that some local bagging companies are underfilling the 50kg bags of cement they sell to the public by bagging 41-48 kg and passing them off as 50kg bags, a practice they consider to be cheating and a violation of market rules.

a3338.speaker: Ministry of Trade of The Gambia
a3338.name: Ministry of Trade of The Gambia
a3338.speech: Has ordered Jah Oil to repackage its products after being found guilty of underfilling the 50 kg bags of cement.

a3338.speaker: Gambia Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (GCCPC)
a3338.name: Gambia Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (GCCPC)
a3338.speech: Warned those involved in the practice to stop such illegal activities.

a3338.speaker: Many other truck drivers found at the company's outside gates
a3338.name: Many other truck drivers found at the company's outside gates
a3338.speech: Explained similar stories, calling on the Gambia Government, especially the Ministry of Trade, to intervene and address the situation.

a3419.speaker: Haas (Formula One team)
a3419.name: Haas (Formula One team)
a3419.speech: Said the 39-year-old, who raced for the US-owned team for five seasons, would test a 2023 Haas VF-23 at the Mugello circuit.

a3419.speaker: Romain Grosjean, former Haas Formula One driver (statement)
a3419.name: Romain Grosjean
a3419.title: former Haas Formula One driver (statement)
a3419.speech: "To say I'm excited to get back behind the wheel of a Formula One car would naturally be an understatement." ; "I really can't believe it's been almost five years, but to come back and have this outing with my old team is truly something special." ; "My kids had designed my helmet for what was meant to be my final grand prix in Abu Dhabi back in 2020 - I'm at last going to be able to give it a go in a Formula One car on Friday."

a3419.speaker: Romain Grosjean, former Haas Formula One driver
a3419.name: Romain Grosjean
a3419.title: former Haas Formula One driver
a3419.speech: Said later that he thought he was going to die in the 2020 Bahrain crash but willed himself out of the inferno for the sake of his children.

a3419.speaker: Ayao Komatsu, Haas team principal (statement)
a3419.name: Ayao Komatsu
a3419.title: Haas team principal (statement)
a3419.speech: "I'm absolutely thrilled to be welcoming Romain Grosjean back into a Formula One car for the first time in five years but especially proud he's returning in one of our cars - it's only fitting." ; "I'm delighted he embraced the opportunity to come and get back behind the wheel with us, a day that's going to be made extra special by having so many members of the original crew back together to witness it."

a3482.speaker: Edward Kallon, UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator
a3482.name: Edward Kallon
a3482.title: UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator
a3482.speech: Said Zimbabwe needs to come up with innovative financing solutions to enhance domestic resource mobilisation amid rising health demands, such as for anti-retroviral drugs.

a3521.speaker: Bola Ahmed Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a3521.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
a3521.title: President of Nigeria
a3521.speech: Has directed the National Single Window (NSW) Steering Committee to ensure that the digital trade facilitation platform becomes fully operational by the first quarter of 2026; the directive was delivered at the fifth Steering Committee meeting, where he was represented by his Chief of Staff.

a3521.speaker: Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy (statement)
a3521.name: Bayo Onanuga
a3521.title: Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy (statement)
a3521.speech: Signed a statement on Tuesday conveying that the President’s directive was delivered at the fifth Steering Committee meeting held at the State House, Abuja, where he was represented by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

a3521.speaker: Femi Gbajabiamila, Chief of Staff to the President
a3521.name: Femi Gbajabiamila
a3521.title: Chief of Staff to the President
a3521.speech: Noted that the recent Tax Reform Act, signed into law in June, had added urgency to Nigeria’s economic reform agenda ; "It's important that we continue to stay focused on this project. So that at the end of the day, we meet our timelines and achieve the results the President expects." ; "As you all are aware, the project is one of the transformative initiatives of Mr. President which we collectively must ensure is effectively and commendably implemented." ; emphasised that the NSW would simplify Nigeria’s import and export operations, boost trade revenue, improve transparency, and enhance the country’s global business credibility ; "I do expect that since the last meeting of the steering committee which was held on the 8th April, 2025, all stakeholders have operated and actively progressed with all the required KPIs and set targets to ensure that we go live with phase 1 in Q1 2026 as was previously scheduled."

a3521.speaker: Wale Edun, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3521.name: Wale Edun
a3521.title: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3521.speech: Described the project’s progress as encouraging but emphasized the need to move from strategy to implementation; described the project as "complex but transformational," and called for stronger collaboration to overcome the remaining hurdles and meet the rollout deadline.

a3521.speaker: Jumoke Oduwole, Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment
a3521.name: Jumoke Oduwole
a3521.title: Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment
a3521.speech: Charged the steering committee to work diligently and ensure that the Phase 1 launch happens in Q1 2026 "without fail."

a3521.speaker: Zacch Adedeji, Executive Chairman of the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS)
a3521.name: Zacch Adedeji
a3521.title: Executive Chairman of the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS)
a3521.speech: Thanked the President for his consistent support of the initiative: "Thank you on behalf of the steering committee. We thank you for the relentless support that you have given to us." ; "And to all my colleagues here, we can see that the reward for hard work is more work. When we started last month, it is now law; the single window is now in the law," urging committee members to remain focused on the mission ahead.

a3521.speaker: Tola Fakolade, Director of the NSW Project
a3521.name: Tola Fakolade
a3521.title: Director of the NSW Project
a3521.speech: Provided a brief update on the committee’s progress and assured that the Q1 2026 deadline remains achievable: "All second quarter 2025 key project milestones have been successfully achieved. And the customisation of the Single Window platform has commenced."

a3748.speaker: French presidency (statement)
a3748.name: French presidency (statement)
a3748.speech: Said countries including France, Kenya, Barbados and Spain launched a coalition to push for taxes on wealthy air passengers to help poorer nations respond to climate change ; said in a statement ahead of November's UN climate summit in Brazil that the group would work on making the aviation sector contribute more to funding climate adaptation, and that the aim would be to plough at least some of the tax proceeds into “resilient investments and fair transitions” and help poorer countries raise more domestic revenue, a key factor for development.

a3748.speaker: The eight-country coalition
a3748.name: The eight-country coalition
a3748.speech: Said it would work to increase the number of countries taxing plane tickets, including business-class travel, and private jets ; has suggested levies on flying could raise up to 187 billion euros ($220 billion) if they were applied across the board.

a3748.speaker: Greenpeace
a3748.name: Greenpeace
a3748.speech: Welcomed an “important step” to raise more money from “the most elite and polluting form of travel”, which has remained “undertaxed”.

a3748.speaker: Rebecca Newsom, Greenpeace's global political lead
a3748.name: Rebecca Newsom
a3748.title: Greenpeace's global political lead
a3748.speech: “Bold, cooperative action that makes polluters pay is not just fair — it's essential,” said in a statement.

a3788.speaker: J. Cyrus Saygbe, Sr., Private Sector Advisor at USAID Liberia
a3788.name: J. Cyrus Saygbe
a3788.title: Sr., Private Sector Advisor at USAID Liberia
a3788.speech: Emphasized the U.S. Government's dedication to empowering Liberian businesses as engines of sustainable growth and its commitment to fostering economic growth and supporting Liberia’s private sector: “This competition is a testament to the U.S. Government’s commitment to investing in Liberia’s private sector, fostering sustainability, and building a more prosperous future for all” ; “This competition celebrates the innovation, ambition, and resilience of Liberia’s agribusinesses. Together, we are transforming Liberia’s agricultural sector into a commercialized driver of growth and opportunity.”

a3788.speaker: Akouavi Tehounge, CEO and Founder of Jimmy Snacks Kitchen
a3788.name: Akouavi Tehounge
a3788.title: CEO and Founder of Jimmy Snacks Kitchen
a3788.speech: “I am so excited! This is my first significant funding win. In the coming months, as we secure the funds, we plan to scale our business, create more jobs, and ensure our products reach every county in Liberia.”

a3842.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.name: Prosper Bazombanza
a3842.title: Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.speech: Said the meeting, chaired by Kenyan President William Ruto, the current AU chairman, was held in order to inaugurate the special committee of Heads of State and Government overseeing the institutional reforms of the African Union.

a3842.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.name: Prosper Bazombanza
a3842.title: Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.speech: In his speech on behalf of the Burundian Head of State: "The will of the Heads of State and Government to reform our African Union in depth reflects a shared aspiration to endow our continent with strong, coherent institutions adapted to the challenges of the 21st century. These reforms are the foundation on which the realisation of Agenda 2063 rests, that of an integrated, prosperous and peaceful Africa, an Africa that we want, an Africa that we must build together."

a3842.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.name: Prosper Bazombanza
a3842.title: Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.speech: Affirmed that Burundi firmly supports the reform of the African Union's financing system, stating that the organisation's budgetary autonomy is the only key to its independence and credibility, and indicated that the effective implementation of the 0.2% levy on eligible imports is crucial to guarantee the financial independence of the African Union, as well as its political sovereignty and freedom of action ; Mentioned that the main objective of the reform is to ensure the financial sovereignty of the continent in order to build together an African Union worthy of its ideals, at the service of its peoples, an African Union of dignity, results and hope.

a3842.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.name: Prosper Bazombanza
a3842.title: Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.speech: "Today, our organisation is evolving in a world confronted with multiple crises of political instability, security threats, climate change, economic and social challenges. These trials undermine the resilience and credibility of our organisation. And yet, it is in these moments of challenge that our determination must assert itself. And whatever the situation, we must build a more robust African Union, capable of acting quickly and effectively to defend the principles of its constitutive Charter." ; Insisted that AU member states must rationalise their institutions, eliminate duplication and optimise the use of their own resources, because a Union that depends too much on external financing risks losing its freedom of decision ; "That is why we must redouble our efforts to strengthen our autonomy, while consolidating coordination between the Commission, the Regional Economic Communities and the member states." ; Underlined that the simplification of the AU's structures is an imperative for an African Union worthy of its ambitions.

a3842.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.name: Prosper Bazombanza
a3842.title: Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
a3842.speech: "And the government of Burundi, through the leadership of President Evariste Ndayishimiye, commits to contributing actively to this process, convinced that an effective, financially autonomous and strategically coherent African Union is the indispensable condition for our shared ambition, that of a sovereign, respected and influential Africa on the world stage."

a3941.speaker: National Health Department presentation documents (private meeting with Pepfar, September), obtained by Spotlight and GroundUp
a3941.name: National Health Department presentation documents (private meeting with Pepfar
a3941.title: September), obtained by Spotlight and GroundUp
a3941.speech: Show that in 2024 the US funded nearly half of all lay counsellors working in South Africa’s public primary healthcare system – 1 931 counsellors across the country (excluding the Northern Cape) ; show Pepfar also funded nearly half of all data capturers, amounting to 2 669 people.

a3941.speaker: South African National Health Department
a3941.name: South African National Health Department
a3941.speech: Has tried to reassure the public that the country’s HIV response is mostly funded by the government, with 17% funded by Pepfar – currently about R7.5 billion a year.

a3941.speaker: A doctor at a large public hospital in Johannesburg (anonymous)
a3941.name: A doctor at a large public hospital in Johannesburg (anonymous)
a3941.speech: Told Spotlight and GroundUp that “USAID covered a substantial proportion… of the doctors, counsellors, clerks, and other administrative personnel [in the hospital’s HIV clinic]. All have either had their contracts terminated or are in the process of doing so” ; said the clinic lost eight counsellors, eight data capturers, a clinical manager and a medical officer, representing half of the clinic’s doctors and counsellors and about 80% of the data capturers ; “There was no warning about this, had we had time, we could have made contingency plans and things wouldn’t be so bad… But if it happens literally overnight, it’s extremely unfair on the patients and remaining staff. The loss of capacity is significant” ; said nurses have started to take on tasks previously performed by counsellors, such as HIV testing, but services haven’t recovered fully and things were still “chaotic”: “It’s not as if the department has any excess capacity, so [when] nurses are diverted to do the testing and counselling, then other parts of care suffer.”

a3941.speaker: Professor Francois Venter, head of the Ezintsha research centre at WITS university
a3941.name: Professor Francois Venter
a3941.title: head of the Ezintsha research centre at WITS university
a3941.speech: Argued that Pepfar programmes were comparatively efficient because they were run by NGOs that needed to compete for US funding: “Pepfar is a monster to work for… They put targets in front of these organisations and say, ‘if you don’t meet them in the next month, we’ll just give the money to your competitors’ and you’ll be out on the streets… So there’s no messing around” ; said US funding agencies would closely monitor progress to see if organisations were meeting targets ; “You don’t see that with the rest of the healthcare system, which just bumbles along with no real metrics” ; “The health system in South Africa, like most health systems, is not terribly well monitored or well directed. When you look at what you get with every single health dollar spent on the Pepfar programme, it’s incredibly good value for money.”

a3941.speaker: Professor Francois Venter, head of the Ezintsha research centre at WITS university
a3941.name: Professor Francois Venter
a3941.title: head of the Ezintsha research centre at WITS university
a3941.speech: On key populations losing services: “This meant… we had to deal with violence issues, we had to deal with the brothel owners, and work out which days of the week, and hours of the day we could provide the care. Logistically, it’s much more complex than sitting on your bum and waiting for them to come and visit you at the clinic. So you can put up your hand and say: ‘oh they can just come to the clinics’ - like the minister said - well, then you won’t be treating any sex workers” ; said this would result in a “public health disaster” ; argued that one of the most crucial services key populations may lose access to is pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).

a3941.speaker: Lynne Wilkinson, public health specialist
a3941.name: Lynne Wilkinson
a3941.title: public health specialist
a3941.speech: Provided the example of the differentiated service delivery programme, explaining that once patients are clinically stable and virally suppressed they don’t need to pick up their ARVs from a health facility each month, but noted that before someone can be enrolled clinicians need to check eligibility: “Because [the enrolment process] was going very slowly… this was supplemented by Pepfar-funded clinicians who would go into a clinic and review a lot of clients and get them into that system” ; said Pepfar-funded staff successfully resolved a major bottleneck in the system, reducing the number of people in clinics and cutting down on waiting times.

a3941.speaker: Lynne Wilkinson, public health specialist
a3941.name: Lynne Wilkinson
a3941.title: public health specialist
a3941.speech: Said the Pepfar grants of most CDC-funded organisations come to an end in September, and for some the money stops at the end of this month.

a3941.speaker: Dr Yogan Pillay, former deputy director of the national health department, now director for HIV and TB delivery at the Gates Foundation
a3941.name: Dr Yogan Pillay
a3941.title: former deputy director of the national health department, now director for HIV and TB delivery at the Gates Foundation
a3941.speech: Told Spotlight and GroundUp that we don’t have data on how efficient Pepfar programmes are at the national level, and argued this needs to be investigated before the health department spends its limited resources trying to revive or replicate the programmes ; said many Pepfar-funded initiatives were providing crucial services, but argued that “the management structure of the [recipient] NGOs is too top-heavy and too expensive” for the government to fund, and that we need to consider and evaluate a variety of HIV delivery models instead of rushing to replicate the Pepfar ones.

a3941.speaker: 2024 report by Ritshidze (health system monitoring organisation)
a3941.name: 2024 report by Ritshidze (health system monitoring organisation)
a3941.speech: Found that around 90% of surveyed sex workers say staff at key populations centres are always friendly and professional, while only a quarter feel the same way about staff at government clinics, and that many key populations are mistreated and discriminated against at public health facilities.

a3941.speaker: South African National Health Department
a3941.name: South African National Health Department
a3941.speech: Has urged patients that were relying on USAID-funded key populations services to go to government health facilities.

a3941.speaker: Survey of people at high risk of contracting HIV in KwaZulu-Natal
a3941.name: Survey of people at high risk of contracting HIV in KwaZulu-Natal
a3941.speech: Found that only 15% were even aware that their clinic stocked PrEP.

a3941.speaker: Another large survey
a3941.name: Another large survey
a3941.speech: Found that at government facilities only 19% of sex workers had been offered PrEP, while at drop-in centres for key populations the figure was more than double, at 40%.

a3941.speaker: A health department official (anonymous)
a3941.name: A health department official (anonymous)
a3941.speech: Told Spotlight and GroundUp that the bulk of the PrEP rollout would continue despite the US funding cuts: “The majority of the PrEP is offered through the [government] clinics,” 96% of which have the drug ; conceded that specific high-risk groups like sex workers have primarily gotten PrEP from the key populations centres rather than the clinics: “This is the biggest area where we are going to see a major decline in uptake for [PrEP] services.”

a3941.speaker: Modelling study published in the Annals of Medicine
a3941.name: Modelling study published in the Annals of Medicine
a3941.speech: Found that the complete loss of all Pepfar funds could lead to over 600 000 deaths in South Africa over the next decade.

a3941.speaker: Foster Mohale, spokesperson for the South African health department
a3941.name: Foster Mohale
a3941.title: spokesperson for the South African health department
a3941.speech: Responded to questions about whether the health department would be supporting key populations centres, and when pressed for details about the department’s plans for dealing with the US cuts simply said they could not reveal specifics at this stage and that “this is a work in progress.”

a3941.speaker: Enoch Godongwana, South African Finance Minister
a3941.name: Enoch Godongwana
a3941.title: South African Finance Minister
a3941.speech: In his budget speech in Parliament on Wednesday did not announce any funding to cover the gap left by the abrupt end of US support for the country’s HIV response ; prior to the speech told reporters in a briefing that the health department would assist with some of the shortfall, but no further information could be provided.

a4315.speaker: Joan Chamungu, Tanzania Network of Women Living with HIV, representative of the African networks of people living with HIV/AIDS
a4315.name: Joan Chamungu
a4315.title: Tanzania Network of Women Living with HIV, representative of the African networks of people living with HIV/AIDS
a4315.speech: said, “We, as an African network of people living with HIV, seek resources and commitment in the fight to end HIV. We are grateful for the efforts made by our governments to advance gains in the HIV response. It is encouraging to see our governments playing a crucial role in combating the pandemic,” ; “We commend their efforts to increase domestic funding, contribute to global initiatives like the Global Fund for AIDS, TB, and Malaria, and develop inclusive, sustainable roadmaps for tackling HIV in our countries.”

a4315.speaker: Joan Chamungu, Tanzania Network of Women Living with HIV
a4315.name: Joan Chamungu
a4315.title: Tanzania Network of Women Living with HIV
a4315.speech: Commended all African governments for ensuring that key populations are included in national HIV strategies by widening access to HIV services and decriminalising key populations, and expressed gratitude to the German and European communities: “As the community of African people living with HIV, we appreciate the support received from Germany, the European Union, and the global community in strengthening intergenerational life-saving systems for people living with HIV in our countries,” ; “Through this support, transmission of HIV from mothers to children is on the verge of being eliminated. Moreover, this support has allowed children born with HIV to grow to adulthood and have their children. In the past, HIV was a death sentence; now, people can enjoy their full lives, thanks to remarkable global solidarity.”

a4315.speaker: German Chancellor
a4315.name: German Chancellor
a4315.speech: Reiterated Germany’s commitment to the global fight against the AIDS pandemic at the International AIDS Conference.

a4315.speaker: African networks of people living with HIV (collective statement)
a4315.name: African networks of people living with HIV (collective statement)
a4315.speech: “Resources provided to the Global Fund, the World Health Organisation, and other multilateral health institutions have led to substantial gains in the fight against HIV,” the African PLHIV networks said, thanking the European and international communities for their support; the community also acknowledged the impact of the U.S. government’s PEPFAR initiative, saying that their powerful program has played a transformative role in the global HIV epidemic landscape.

a4315.speaker: African networks of people living with HIV (collective statement)
a4315.name: African networks of people living with HIV (collective statement)
a4315.speech: Have become increasingly worried by falling international funding for the HIV response and stress that “more resources need to be allocated to deal with all the gaps in this fight,” emphasising that now is a critical time for additional support ; noted that the threat to PEPFAR’s five-year reauthorisation cycle can disrupt national program planning as well as undermine congressional support, and pointed out the troubling trend of some governments criminalising communities most affected by HIV.

a4315.speaker: David Kamkwamba, Network of Journalists Living with HIV (JONEHA) Malawi
a4315.name: David Kamkwamba
a4315.title: Network of Journalists Living with HIV (JONEHA) Malawi
a4315.speech: Highlighted the impact of PEPFAR and international support to strengthen procurement power within African countries, saying it has scaled up treatment and prevention, reduced major gaps in human resources, strengthened community health systems, and addressed rights violations and structural barriers to accessing health services through programs like DREAMS and community-led monitoring (CLM) ; “These are our humble ask. To address the gaps in HIV prevention, we implore Germany, the European community, and the international community to allocate additional resources. We call on both parties in the U.S. Congress to support a clean five-year reauthorisation of PEPFAR, which is essential for achieving the ambitious goal of reducing the burden of HIV by 2030. A failure to secure this reauthorization would signify a retreat in American leadership, with significant repercussions not only for Africa but for the global community as well.”

a4315.speaker: David Kamkwamba, Network of Journalists Living with HIV (JONEHA) Malawi
a4315.name: David Kamkwamba
a4315.title: Network of Journalists Living with HIV (JONEHA) Malawi
a4315.speech: “We strongly urge our governments to further increase domestic funding for strengthening the local sustainability of the response and to address the 10-10-10 gaps,” ensuring the elimination of structural barriers and rights violations faced by those most impacted by HIV.

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said on accountability and divestment that “Accountability is a basic principle of good governance. We are redefining our approach with International Oil and Gas companies, including governments, the private sector, to become less bureaucratic and more agile, effective and efficient”, that the major task before PENGASSAN leadership was how to protect the jobs of members and the existing collective bargaining agreement, and that the association has concluded agreements covering the NAOC–Oando divestment, the Mobil Producing Nigeria–Seplat divestment and the Equinor–Chappal Energy divestment, while stopping all conversations with Shell over the SPDC–Renaissance sale because government declined approval.

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said the leadership of the association across all levels has been engaging different managements at all sub-sectoral levels in negotiating new collective bargaining agreements, and that “We have been able to secure a cumulative increase of 150% to over 200% increment for our members in some branches.”

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said the oil and gas sector faces immense challenges that threaten not only its sustainability but also the prosperity of the nation, that “the challenges facing Nigeria’s oil and gas industry are multifaceted and deeply intertwined with our social, economic, and environmental fabric”, but that these challenges can be turned into opportunities through a commitment to transparency, inclusivity, and innovation.

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said on host communities that harnessing Nigeria’s environmental protection regulations requires a multi-faceted approach focusing on regulatory enforcement, community engagement, proactive environmental management and legal framework enhancement, so that regulations translate into tangible improvements and end youth restiveness and communal conflicts, and called “for a 100% implementation of the provision of host communities in the Petroleum Industry Act.”

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said on the tax reforms that tax relief exemptions given to those earning minimum wage and businesses should be expanded, that clarity must be provided regarding revenue collection processes from oil and gas companies because some provisions could negatively impact members in branches like NUPRC and NMDPRA, and called on the National Assembly “to conduct a proper public hearing session where different views will be collated to amend the provisions in the bill and not just to tick the box.”

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said Nigeria faces a looming food crisis of immense proportions and that PENGASSAN demands the government support both commercial and smallholder farmers through access to credit, improved seeds, fertilisers and technology, strengthening farmer cooperatives and market linkages, investing in roads, storage facilities and irrigation to reduce post-harvest losses, and providing a secure environment enabling farmers who abandoned their farms to return.

a4320.speaker: Cadre Harmonisé Report for October 2024
a4320.name: Cadre Harmonisé Report for October 2024
a4320.speech: Recently projected that at least 33.1 million people in 26 states and the FCT will face a food and nutrition crisis between June and August 2025.

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said on the power sector that Nigeria’s continuous decline in power generation and transmission is profoundly disappointing and a significant cause of the terrible quality of life and economic downturn, that despite tariff increases “we have witnessed the national grid collapse over 6 times this year alone… the worst frequency in our country’s history”, and that the union advocates decentralising power transmission and involving state governments and private sector players, citing Abia State as a good example.

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said on economic policy that there must be information-sharing with stakeholders, especially civil society organisations working on financial management, criticising that countries go to the IMF and World Bank for loans approved without details or oversight of implementation; called for serious reforms for economic stability, noting corruption-driven backsliding, factory closures, failure to collect revenue from multinational corporations and wealthy individuals, absence of property taxation, and dilapidation of health, education and physical infrastructure through diversion and theft of public funds, and said it is important that the IMF/World Bank democratise information and create opportunities for interaction.

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said investment and employment in Nigeria are constrained by high cost and difficulty of accessing credit, problems securing property rights and enforcing contracts, weak energy, transport and communications infrastructure, business registration delays, lack of transparency in regulation and deficiencies in education and skills; that most Nigerian enterprises, many operated by women, remain trapped in the informal economy; and that Nigeria needs a strategy for sustainable enterprise development and decent work including an enabling environment, a better investment climate, macroeconomic stability, respect for workers’ rights, good governance and particular attention to MSMEs and women’s entrepreneurship.

a4320.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.name: Festus Osifo
a4320.title: National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
a4320.speech: Said the urgency of the ‘Africa Solution To African Problems’ quest comes from optimism that Africa’s growth can be led by young people, that timely investment in education and health can spur a demographic dividend since by 2075 one-third of the world’s population and working-age population will be African, that Africa’s Heads of State need to accelerate human capital accumulation, leverage the youth bulge and create jobs, and that Africa is battling a learning crisis with the percentage of 10-year-olds unable to understand a simple text projected to approach 89% after the COVID pandemic.

a4439.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), Regional Economic Outlook report "Holding the Ground"
a4439.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4439.title: Regional Economic Outlook report "Holding the Ground"
a4439.speech: According to the latest Regional Economic Outlook, Sub-Saharan Africa is expected to demonstrate significant economic resilience, achieving an average growth rate of 4.1% in 2025, with growth projected to rebound slightly further in 2026 ; The IMF suggests the sub-region still has room for strength, provided it intensifies its domestic resource mobilization efforts and significantly improves debt management ; The report applauds the region's resilience in the face of major global challenges, including low oil prices, declining development assistance, and tighter borrowing conditions.

a4439.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), Regional Economic Outlook report "Holding the Ground"
a4439.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4439.title: Regional Economic Outlook report "Holding the Ground"
a4439.speech: Cautions that this strength "cannot be taken for granted," highlighting significant macroeconomic vulnerabilities ; The institution warns that "most countries in the region face a combination of fiscal, monetary, and external risks," with twenty countries already classified as being in debt distress or at high risk of debt distress.

a4439.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), Regional Economic Outlook report "Holding the Ground"
a4439.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4439.title: Regional Economic Outlook report "Holding the Ground"
a4439.speech: The report identifies two major priorities essential for strengthening macroeconomic stability: governments must raise more internal revenue by digitizing tax administrations, reducing exemptions, and broadening the tax base, and more transparent and rigorous public debt management is crucial to restoring investor confidence and lowering high borrowing costs ; The IMF also encourages the use of innovative financing instruments, such as blended finance mechanisms and debt-for-development swaps, while simultaneously urging governments to strengthen governance and fiscal transparency ; The report concludes by stressing the need for balance: "In a context of persistent uncertainty, countries must preserve macroeconomic stability while pursuing their development objectives."

a4455.speaker: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré, President of Burkina Faso
a4455.name: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré
a4455.title: President of Burkina Faso
a4455.speech: Hammered the day after a terrorist attack at Koutoukou: "Burkina will not yield in the face of terrorism, even if we all have to lose our lives doing so."

a4455.speaker: Simon Compaoré, president of the People's Movement for Progress (MPP), the ruling party
a4455.name: Simon Compaoré
a4455.title: president of the People's Movement for Progress (MPP), the ruling party
a4455.speech: Proclaims proudly of the microcredit policy for women: "This has made it possible to sow hope in the hearts of millions of Burkinabè."

a4455.speaker: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré, President of Burkina Faso
a4455.name: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré
a4455.title: President of Burkina Faso
a4455.speech: According to the President of Burkina Faso, at the inauguration of the Samendeni dam, its operation will generate GDP growth of nearly 2% and an increase in national cereal production of nearly 3%, as well as the creation of at least 100,000 jobs.

a4455.speaker: Mathias Somé, head of the Monitoring Bureau (Bureau de suivi) of the presidential programme
a4455.name: Mathias Somé
a4455.title: head of the Monitoring Bureau (Bureau de suivi) of the presidential programme
a4455.speech: In a three-question interview: "The most important thing is to work for the well-being of the people"; said the Head of State's priorities for the five-year term were to modernise the administration, to work on human capital, and to work on the sectors that will develop the economy and create jobs.

a4455.speaker: Mathias Somé, head of the Monitoring Bureau (Bureau de suivi) of the presidential programme
a4455.name: Mathias Somé
a4455.title: head of the Monitoring Bureau (Bureau de suivi) of the presidential programme
a4455.speech: Said the five-year term took place in a difficult context marked by insecurity nobody saw coming, an inherited fragile budget from commitments made by the previous transitional government, and social revolt; yet the regime made achievements in health (free care for children 0-5 and for women, work towards universal health insurance), infrastructure in urban and rural areas, and education, building large numbers of solid classrooms in place of straw-hut schools.

a4455.speaker: Mathias Somé, head of the Monitoring Bureau (Bureau de suivi) of the presidential programme
a4455.name: Mathias Somé
a4455.title: head of the Monitoring Bureau (Bureau de suivi) of the presidential programme
a4455.speech: Explained that the Bureau's role is to see with ministries which actions fit the priority actions and to design monitoring mechanisms, including strengthening a culture of accountability; said the Bureau is building an information system on development operations so citizens can follow the impact of government action, and that of the 626 commitments in the government action programme, 147 "transfer commitments" were selected across six key fields - education, health, water, energy, agriculture and infrastructure - which allowed convincing results in all sectors.

a4455.speaker: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré, President of Burkina Faso (quoted by Mathias Somé)
a4455.name: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré
a4455.title: President of Burkina Faso (quoted by Mathias Somé)
a4455.speech: The Head of State said: "whether you are appointed or elected, you must know that you must render accounts to those you administer, to the partners who accompany us, and also put in place good governance. The citizen must know what you are doing for his good and how you are doing it, and he can call you to account."

a4455.speaker: Simon Compaoré, president of the People's Movement for Progress (MPP), the ruling party
a4455.name: Simon Compaoré
a4455.title: president of the People's Movement for Progress (MPP), the ruling party
a4455.speech: "The roar of machines all day long since our accession to power amply demonstrates that our country is one vast permanent building site. In the space of 5 years, tarred roads have been built all over Burkina Faso, rural roads rehabilitated or created to facilitate the mobility of our brave rural populations; more than 1,000 kilometres of asphalt have been laid, or are being built."

a4455.speaker: Jean Wenceslas Kyelem, director general of Road Infrastructure, Ministry of Infrastructure
a4455.name: Jean Wenceslas Kyelem
a4455.title: director general of Road Infrastructure, Ministry of Infrastructure
a4455.speech: Said the Boromo bridge is the first mixed steel-concrete bridge in Burkina, being composed of a reinforced concrete deck resting on a metal framework of 180 tonnes.

a4455.speaker: Wilfried Yaméogo, director general of Sofitex (Burkinabè Textile Fibre Company)
a4455.name: Wilfried Yaméogo
a4455.title: director general of Sofitex (Burkinabè Textile Fibre Company)
a4455.speech: Welcomes the government measures taken to boost the cotton sector, strategic for the Burkinabè economy, which according to him has never been in such good health.

a4692.speaker: Dr. Ernest Kombo, President of the Africa Hope Development Foundation
a4692.name: Dr. Ernest Kombo
a4692.title: President of the Africa Hope Development Foundation
a4692.speech: Said widows, widowers, and other vulnerable citizens need support and love ; pledged his organisation to assist the needy households and refugees flocking to Namibia through the Katima Mulilo Border Post, as well as widows ; "Therefore, it is imperative and incumbent upon us that we exert ourselves in helping our beneficiaries to be strengthened in their areas of need, so as to enable them to be responsible enough to sustain themselves while maintaining their dignity and self-worth."

a4692.speaker: Moffat Sileze, Swapo Party Coordinator for the Zambezi Region
a4692.name: Moffat Sileze
a4692.title: Swapo Party Coordinator for the Zambezi Region
a4692.speech: Lauded the Foundation for helping the needy.

a4764.speaker: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis, Minister in charge of Decentralisation
a4764.name: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis
a4764.title: Minister in charge of Decentralisation
a4764.speech: In his speech thanked first of all the 5 presidents of regional councils for having taken the time to participate fully in the work of this cluster; he also thanked the development partners for their total involvement in the work of the cluster, of which they are an integral part, and underlined their active role in the implementation of the decentralisation policy.

a4764.speaker: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis, Minister in charge of Decentralisation
a4764.name: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis
a4764.title: Minister in charge of Decentralisation
a4764.speech: Affirmed that the meeting of this cluster coordination group, bringing together the institutional actors of decentralisation, the international partners and the actors of the local authorities, constitutes a long-awaited exercise for his department ; “Its objective is to exchange jointly and fully on the initiatives of each actor, to make such a Group a useful space for exchange and progress, because one of the major challenges of decentralisation is the success of the coordination process between the actors concerned and the various stakeholders” ; “For our department it is a matter of avoiding duplication, of harmonising both the approaches and of weighing together the means and the initiatives deployed or to be programmed in each region.”

a4764.speaker: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis, Minister in charge of Decentralisation
a4764.name: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis
a4764.title: Minister in charge of Decentralisation
a4764.speech: Highlighted the need to make the meetings of such a Cluster permanent, to make it a platform whose meetings are formalised and standardised for optimal effectiveness; specified that his department, supported by the Expertise France Agency, will play a pivotal technical role in the conduct of these meetings and in the support provided to each local authority ; insisted that the framework for these meetings be set quickly, so that each stakeholder takes into consideration its role and responsibilities.

a4764.speaker: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis, Minister in charge of Decentralisation
a4764.name: Hamadou Mohamed Aramis
a4764.title: Minister in charge of Decentralisation
