a4764.speech: Recalled that developing the potential of each region is at the heart of the policy of the government of President Ismail Omar Guelleh, with a view to promoting balanced and sustainable development of the regions; said it is a question of correcting the unbalanced development between Djibouti city and the interior regions inherited from the colonial period and thereby fighting the rural exodus ; asked the presidents of the regions to reflect on job-creating projects in line with current government policy and invited the development partners to help them with expertise and with the mobilisation of financing.

a4764.speaker: Mohamed Ali Hassan, Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a4764.name: Mohamed Ali Hassan
a4764.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a4764.speech: Underlined in his address that his department provides its support to this meeting but also to all the activities that the government carries out through the secretary of state within the framework of the policy of decentralisation and deconcentration ; “We will always continue, within the framework of the foreign policy and the development aid policy that we conduct, to pursue the mobilisation of the financial, human and material means necessary to accompany you, Mr Minister of Decentralisation, in the implementation of the decentralisation and deconcentration programme. You can count on the full support of the ministry of foreign affairs and international cooperation” ; underlined that this cluster is a very appropriate mechanism for monitoring and for the establishment of an inclusive dialogue, and certainly the best tool for all the programmes the decentralisation department will carry out ; expressed to the partners the gratitude of the government and issued a call to the development partners to continue the work of mobilising resources alongside the secretariat of state in charge of decentralisation.

a4764.speaker: Development partners (EU delegation, UNDP, WFP, FAO, USAID, UNICEF, AFD, GIZ)
a4764.name: Development partners (EU delegation
a4764.title: UNDP, WFP, FAO, USAID, UNICEF, AFD, GIZ)
a4764.speech: Congratulated the minister in charge of decentralisation for the initiative of setting up a decentralisation cluster group, “a mechanism, according to them, that is very appropriate for inclusive dialogue and for strengthening partnership in order to respond as best as possible to the aspirations for the well-being of our compatriots wherever they may be” ; assured the minister of their readiness to accompany his department in all its efforts.

a4764.speaker: Participants of the meeting (recommendations)
a4764.name: Participants of the meeting (recommendations)
a4764.speech: Affirmed in their recommendations that they shared with Minister Hamadou Mohamed Aramis the need to hold such meetings regularly so that they can serve as a permanent platform of consultation and dialogue between the national institutions, the territorial authorities and the technical and financial partners ; expressed their adherence to Minister Aramis’s suggestion of seeing this kind of meeting replicated at the level of each region, in order to begin a dialogue on questions of governance and local development.

a4781.speaker: Chipoka Mulenga, Zambian Commerce, Trade and Industry Minister
a4781.name: Chipoka Mulenga
a4781.title: Zambian Commerce, Trade and Industry Minister
a4781.speech: Has said that cooperating partners withdrawing support from Zambia due to challenges is not a punishment to the ruling party, but to the people, a move that contradicts the core values of the partnership.

a4900.speaker: Desire Sibande, NEGLA North representative
a4900.name: Desire Sibande
a4900.title: NEGLA North representative
a4900.speech: Spoke to Malawi24 about the importance of youth involvement in democracy: “We urge all young people in the district to register in large numbers and vote for leaders of their choice on September 16, 2024,” he said. “We also encourage the youth to run for various leadership positions to bring fresh ideas and energy to our communities.”

a4900.speaker: Pastor Chrispine Chakhumbira, Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) officer for Mzimba South
a4900.name: Pastor Chrispine Chakhumbira
a4900.title: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) officer for Mzimba South
a4900.speech: Announced that voter registration for the district will take place from November 28 to December 11, 2024. “We encourage all eligible voters to visit their local registration centres to register,” Chakhumbira said.

a5004.speaker: Anonymous informant (tip-off to customs)
a5004.name: Anonymous informant (tip-off to customs)
a5004.speech: An anonymous tip-off alerted the customs agents to the suspicious behaviour of three passengers aboard a bus travelling from Bittou to Lome in Togo; the information gathered indicated that these individuals were transporting a large quantity of gold without the legal documents required for its possession or export.

a5004.speaker: Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a5004.name: Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a5004.speech: Hailed this exemplary operation, congratulating the agents involved for their vigilance and professionalism; he also renewed his call for close collaboration between citizens and the security forces in order to fight illicit activities effectively.

a5004.speaker: Directorate General of Customs of Burkina Faso (Customs)
a5004.name: Directorate General of Customs of Burkina Faso (Customs)
a5004.speech: Customs recall that any export of gold must comply with the legal provisions in force, under penalty of severe sanctions.

a5016.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5016.name: Marco Rubio
a5016.title: US Secretary of State
a5016.speech: Says he has sent directives to people deployed abroad so that they be placed on unpaid leave and not dismissed, on unpaid leave as of Friday; according to him, people were trying to use the system to push payments through on the sly and by force despite the suspension order: “So we sent directives to people deployed abroad so that they be placed on unpaid leave and not dismissed, on unpaid leave as of Friday, and we stated it very clearly in the message.” He added that the directives indicate there would be specially designated programmes that would not be part of this order, and emphasised that people had 30 days for his administration to help them return home if they so wished.

a5016.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5016.name: Marco Rubio
a5016.title: US Secretary of State
a5016.speech: Explained that his administration's effort has always been to identify the programmes that work and continue them, and to identify the programmes that are not aligned with the US national interest and deal with them; concluded by assuring that the United States will provide foreign aid, but it will be foreign aid that makes sense and that is aligned with the country's national interest.

a5053.speaker: Kalekeni Kaphale, lawyer for former Finance Minister Joseph Mwanamvekha
a5053.name: Kalekeni Kaphale
a5053.title: lawyer for former Finance Minister Joseph Mwanamvekha
a5053.speech: Has expressed concerns over the charges, seeking clarification on certain aspects before the trial commences ; has dismissed these claims [that Mwanamvekha attempted to sabotage the Salima Sugar Company's operations], stating that they are baseless and lack substance.

a5053.speaker: Sources close to the investigation (anonymous)
a5053.name: Sources close to the investigation (anonymous)
a5053.speech: Have revealed that other high-ranking officials from the DPP administration are also expected to be summoned by the police for questioning.

a5053.speaker: Police officers at Blantyre Police Station (anonymous)
a5053.name: Police officers at Blantyre Police Station (anonymous)
a5053.speech: Were heard expressing support for the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and Sameer Suleiman, echoing the phrase “Boma ndilomweli la DPP li,” which translates to “the government belongs to DPP” ; according to eyewitnesses, the officers were heard saying, “We are just doing our duties because of the orders from above, but boma ndilomweli” ; some officers disclosed that they had received orders from above to oppress Suleiman and ensure that he spends a night in jail.

a5099.speaker: Tim Harford, economist and journalist (‘‘The Undercover Economist’’)
a5099.name: Tim Harford
a5099.title: economist and journalist (‘‘The Undercover Economist’’)
a5099.speech: Opens his book with the example of cappuccino in London: illustrating the miracle of cross-dependencies and co-ordinated actions that bring together finely engineered Italian coffee machines, coffee from Africa, milk from English farms, crockery from China, and so on, into a single cup of exquisite coffee, again, and again.

a5099.speaker: AgResults (project)
a5099.name: AgResults (project)
a5099.speech: A recent project which proved that the answer lies in a remarkable suspension of marketing; it ran a challenge, offering prize money to the producers of simple, low cost, grain storage solutions who could sell the most to smallholders. Last month, three companies were awarded $4m as a result, and nine suppliers who entered the challenge sold enough bags and storage bins in the Rift and Eastern to store an extra 4.6m 90kg bags of maize, saving up to Sh2.2bn in post-harvest losses.

a5099.speaker: Researchers at KALRO
a5099.name: Researchers at KALRO
a5099.speech: Long ago developed a cure for Grain Borer: cheap seeds planted next to the maize attract the pest to lay its eggs, which get stuck to the grass on hatching, so virtually no maize gets eaten. The researchers call it ‘push-pull technology’.

a5204.speaker: Macmillan Anyawu, AfDB Country Manager
a5204.name: Macmillan Anyawu
a5204.title: AfDB Country Manager
a5204.speech: Said the signing of the three agreements demonstrated his bank's continued commitment to supporting and complementing government's efforts to develop the agriculture sector and the economy of Malawi at large: “We therefore look forward to a full implementation of the identified policy reform areas under this budget support and strengthened government capacity to respond to the prevailing climatic shock while building the resilience to climate change in the long term.”

a5204.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Malawi Finance Minister
a5204.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a5204.title: Malawi Finance Minister
a5204.speech: Said the Agriculture Based Budgetary Support was designed to support the implementation of Malawi Government's medium-term development agenda, and that the programme places a strong emphasis on enhancing agricultural productivity, commercialisation and strengthening public finance management: “This budgetary support will help in creating an enabling economic and regulatory environment for agricultural transformation by Promoting agricultural productivity, commercialisation, and market access to help our farmers increase their output and connect to better markets.” ; Added that the signing of the three project agreements represents the collective commitment to driving agricultural transformation, strengthening public financial management and building resilience against the inevitable challenges of tomorrow.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: said Cabo Verde has always performed well on the external front and that, with a new dynamic imprinted on its diplomatic action, its conduct has been quite pragmatic and diligent; she stressed that Cabo Verde has above all safeguarded the defence of internationally recognised values, namely the promotion of international peace and security, international cooperation, solidarity among nations and the defence of human rights, taking positions on the major and most complex questions of the international agenda based on international law and the Charter of the United Nations; she said the country's diplomatic action has increased its visibility abroad and that its contribution has been valuable in peace, international security, development, financing for development and global cross-cutting issues such as climate change, new information and communication technologies and digital governance.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on criticism of Cabo Verde's votes on the Palestinian question, said the criticism is natural in a country where the democratic rule of law prevails and there is full freedom of expression, but that the government's positions have been based above all on the defence of international law and the principles of the UN Charter; she said one must distinguish the Israel-Hamas conflict, that Cabo Verde has chosen to defend international humanitarian law, that it recently subscribed to a Security Council resolution in December calling for better humanitarian assistance in the Gaza Strip and voted in favour of the General Assembly draft resolution recognising that the State of Palestine qualifies for full UN membership and calling on the Security Council to reconsider its position; she said the two abstentions in earlier resolutions had to do with imbalances in the drafting of some provisions, since sustainable solutions require secure foundations; and she stressed that Cabo Verde is an advocate and lover of peace and condemned all terrorist acts, having immediately condemned the attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October as an act of terrorism that should not happen.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on non-alignment, said Cabo Verde is not aligning itself in this conflict and that she can guarantee it, for the simple reason that it defends, and has always defended, the two-State solution — whoever defends the two-State solution is not aligning; she said that essentially all countries on the Security Council abstained on draft resolutions at one moment or another, that abstention does not mean being against the channelling of humanitarian aid, calling that a fallacy and a narrative that must be deconstructed, and stressing that Cabo Verde has opened air corridors so that humanitarian aid reaches Gaza.

a5244.speaker: Dr. Angelo Correia (in an interview with Expresso das Ilhas the previous week)
a5244.name: Dr. Angelo Correia (in an interview with Expresso das Ilhas the previous week)
a5244.speech: said that geopolitics is one of Cabo Verde's great assets.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: agreed that geopolitics is one of Cabo Verde's great assets, saying Cabo Verde has known how to take consistent and coherent positions and that, now more than ever, in a context of growing geopolitical tension, one must analyse and follow the evolution of events and avoid positions that would not help find more sustainable peace solutions; she said that geopolitically Cabo Verde has known how to navigate, with important partnerships with partners of both the North and the South that have projected the country's visibility and role in the international arena, always observing the Constitution of the Republic and the UN Charter.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on Cabo Verde's regional role, said the country is known worldwide for its great democratic stability and for its efforts to strengthen governance, citing a recent conference on Sal island on the importance of democracy, freedom and good governance, which she called Cabo Verde's assets; she said promoting democracy and good governance will help countries find prosperity and sustainable development, that peace, security and development must always be associated ('without peace there is no development, without development there is no peace'), and that in its regional participation Cabo Verde works to ensure democratic institutions are respected and that there is always a peaceful transition of power; she said Cabo Verde vehemently condemns attempted coups d'etat, that the signs of instability in the sub-region are worrying, and that in its dialogues within ECOWAS, and more precisely in the Mediation and Security Council, Cabo Verde always appeals for peace and for constitutional order.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: said ECOWAS has played a quite leading role but obviously cannot do everything alone; there must also be collaboration from political actors and countries, and permanent dialogue with other regional organisations, namely the African Union, and international organisations such as the United Nations; she said what ECOWAS has been doing is basically finding solutions for peace, but that this also requires permanent dialogue between ECOWAS bodies and the countries concerned.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger announcing their withdrawal from ECOWAS, said Cabo Verde has been appealing above all for dialogue, that it is a country which holds that concertation and coordination between countries are the principal path to conflict resolution, and that solutions must also take the other parties into account; she said Cabo Verde has stated categorically that military intervention is never a solution and that other paths must be found, and those other paths must be the path of diplomacy.

a5244.speaker: PAICV (opposition party)
a5244.name: PAICV (opposition party)
a5244.speech: has criticised what it alleges is Cabo Verde's rapprochement with NATO.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on NATO, said it is not a question of membership, since Cabo Verde is in the Mid-Atlantic and NATO is an organisation of North Atlantic countries; she said what Cabo Verde is doing is building a more reinforced partnership, noting that it already had such a partnership with NATO in the 2006 Steadfast Jaguar military exercise, and that it wants to continue that partnership while also taking advantage of NATO's other cooperation instruments with third countries, namely the Global Partner or Individual Partnership, in order to strengthen the country's defence capacity and give technical assistance to national institutions — 'nothing more than that'.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on transnational crime and maritime security, said Cabo Verde has been developing partnerships with partners of both the South and the North, that the country is in a very strategic but high-risk zone given transnational crime, being on the turntable between America, Europe and Africa, and that it is necessary to combat drug trafficking, human trafficking, maritime piracy and illegal fishing and to promote partnerships that reinforce maritime security, since Cabo Verde is a State that is 99.3% sea; she agreed fully that Cabo Verde must keep a vigilant eye given piracy in the Gulf of Guinea, highlighting benefits under the sub-regional SWAIMS project (Support West Africa Integrated Maritime Security) and projects such as Guinex with Brazil, joint surveillance exercises, and noting that Cabo Verde now hosts the Zone G Multinational Maritime Coordination Centre within the Yaounde architecture, a structure that will bring more institutional capacity and foster regional integration in security and defence.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on Morocco and Western Sahara, said Cabo Verde, in its dialogue with the Kingdom of Morocco, has worked so that the autonomy plan is a sustainable solution to the conflict in Western Sahara, noting that the autonomy plan has 35 points and that self-determination is among them, and that there are various theories and concepts of self-determination which need demystifying, what matters being that the international community, under the aegis of the United Nations, finds a solution to the conflict; she said the opening of Cabo Verde's representation in Rabat and in Dakhla is above all about having a greater presence on the African continent, alongside the recent opening of an embassy in Nigeria to reinforce regional integration and the reopening this year of the embassy in Addis Ababa, a strategic point for discussions on the major questions of the African agenda; she said Morocco has been a traditional cooperation partner in different areas and hosts a significant number of students, and that the decision taken in no way violates the Constitution, as was portrayed in the media.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on the financing of embassies, said such financing is very natural in relations between States, that facilities granted by one State for the installation of embassies are very common, that Cabo Verde itself obtained such facilities from other countries in the early days of its independence, and that this in no way violates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations — had it been an unworthy act, the Convention would have stipulated some provision on it; she noted that Cabo Verde has reciprocity agreements on diplomatic properties; and she said greater 'sense of State' must be brought to the management of external relations and the handling of the most sensitive or complex issues of the international agenda, that national consensus is needed for the country to have unity in foreign policy, and that the nation would gain more if it debated foreign policy questions such as development financing, climate change, reform of the international financial architecture, economic diplomacy and sustainable development.

a5244.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.name: Myrian Vieira
a5244.title: Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a5244.speech: on the French elections and the US campaign, said Cabo Verde is obviously following the whole discussion, especially the presidential electoral process in the United States, and is also following the rise of the far right, especially in Europe; she said the concern is above all about the partnership Cabo Verde has with the European Union and about maintaining good relations of cooperation and the special partnership with the EU and its member states; she said the rise of the far right may eventually have impacts on the Cabo Verdean emigrant community, a good part of which is based in European countries, though there are as yet no facts or elements for a precise assessment of what should be done to counter any less positive effect on relations between Cabo Verde and countries with far-right governments or parties; and she stressed that Cabo Verde is a country that always appeals for partnerships and will always be available to maintain good relations of cooperation and friendship with the various European countries.

a5246.speaker: National Planning Commission (NPC) of Malawi
a5246.name: National Planning Commission (NPC) of Malawi
a5246.speech: has said inclusive wealth creation is crucial for achieving Malawi's long-term development vision, Malawi (MW) 2063 ; said this approach was essential for the country's prosperity, as it would enable Malawians to create own wealth and reduce reliance on donor support.

a5246.speaker: Thomas Munthali, Outgoing NPC Director General
a5246.name: Thomas Munthali
a5246.title: Outgoing NPC Director General
a5246.speech: said Malawi must shift focus from relying on foreign aid to creating own wealth: "Our vision is clear; inclusive wealth creation and self-reliance must guide our long-term development. We can no longer rely on donor support. We must create our own wealth. Planning and long-term thinking are important for national development" ; cited several achievements during his time at NPC, including the development of MW 2063 ; urged training institutions such as MSG to align their programmes with goals outlined in MW 2063 ; stressed the need for capacity building to support the national vision, with culture, Tourism, Mining and Manufacturing being prioritized.

a5246.speaker: Jessie Kabwila, Higher Education Minister of Malawi
a5246.name: Jessie Kabwila
a5246.title: Higher Education Minister of Malawi
a5246.speech: said the MW 2063 vision needed to be discussed and known by everyone: "When Malawians understand a certain issue, they are able to implement it. So, we need to explain to everyone what the Malawi 2063 [vision] entails. Malawians have a lot of ideas; we need to engage them to achieve this vision. When implementing it, we need to decentralise it" ; said underprivileged people had good ideas but that they were rarely engaged.

a5246.speaker: Lewis Dzimbiri, MSG (Malawi School of Government) Council Chairperson
a5246.name: Lewis Dzimbiri
a5246.title: MSG (Malawi School of Government) Council Chairperson
a5246.speech: said the goal of becoming a self-reliant nation required more people to be trained in requisite areas: "We can also achieve the Malawi 2063 vision through engagement between the private and public sectors; it is not a one-person job."

a5256.speaker: John Mahama, President of Ghana (statement from the president's office)
a5256.name: John Mahama
a5256.title: President of Ghana (statement from the president's office)
a5256.speech: Has asked Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson to find ways to close the gap in funding left behind by the freeze of USAID programs, according to a statement from the president's office.

a5330.speaker: Dr. Ali Haji Aden, Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Somalia
a5330.name: Dr. Ali Haji Aden
a5330.title: Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Somalia
a5330.speech: Outlined the bill’s provisions to lawmakers, emphasizing its importance to public health; urged parliament to give the draft law thorough consideration, noting that its passage would be crucial for controlling medicine quality and preventing harm caused by substandard pharmaceuticals.

a5330.speaker: Medicine Regulation Bill, introduced by the Ministry of Health (document)
a5330.name: Medicine Regulation Bill
a5330.title: introduced by the Ministry of Health (document)
a5330.speech: Seeks to establish guidelines for importing, distributing, and quality control of medicines; if passed, it would give authorities greater oversight to enforce stricter standards in a largely unregulated market, introducing strict licensing requirements for pharmaceutical imports, mandatory quality testing, and penalties for non-compliance.

a5512.speaker: Dya-Eddin Bamakhrama, Ambassador of Djibouti to Riyadh (opinion column)
a5512.name: Dya-Eddin Bamakhrama
a5512.title: Ambassador of Djibouti to Riyadh (opinion column)
a5512.speech: Argues that alongside conventional diplomacy there exists second-track diplomacy, including humanist diplomacy and popular diplomacy or “soft power”, and that humanist diplomacy is one of the strongest and most effective diplomatic fields, capable of changing the reality on the ground and accomplishing actions sometimes inaccessible to conventional diplomacy ; says that states and decision-making centres continue to play a decisive role in removing the obstacles facing national and international humanitarian organisations, placing their action in an institutional and legal framework and protecting them from security and political infiltration and from corruption ; cites the Republic of Djibouti, which took an early interest in assisting refugees and preserving their dignity - welcoming those fleeing the 1977 Ogaden war despite the modesty of its resources, and today receiving and housing tens of thousands of Yemeni refugees under the personal attention and follow-up of President Ismail Omar Guelleh - and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as a leader in humanist diplomacy, particularly through the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre ; calls for working together to remove obstacles hindering humanitarian action, promote access to zones of conflict, offer more guarantees of protection to humanitarian personnel including diplomatic and political immunities, give increased attention to dialogue and cooperation between humanitarian workers and local authorities, organise forums and workshops for diplomats and humanitarian agents, and give broader space to academic and research efforts to lay the scientific foundations of humanist diplomacy.

a5537.speaker: Dr Hugo Slim, senior researcher at the Las Casas Institute for Social Justice, Oxford
a5537.name: Dr Hugo Slim
a5537.title: senior researcher at the Las Casas Institute for Social Justice, Oxford
a5537.speech: Recalled in his presentation that humanity must act now so that all fight against climate change: significant commitments must be made to protect the future generation, he declared.

a5537.speaker: Dr Hugo Slim, senior researcher at the Las Casas Institute for Social Justice, Oxford
a5537.name: Dr Hugo Slim
a5537.title: senior researcher at the Las Casas Institute for Social Justice, Oxford
a5537.speech: Divided the workshop into three themes: the particular characteristics of climate change that create an emergency for the whole earthly community, including the oceans, pastures, humans, animals, insects and trees; the importance of landscape and mobility for all forms of life on earth, drawing on the environmental expertise of local communities as well as on the Holy Quran to illustrate that survival is a common project between humanity and nature; and, with the stakeholders, whether there exists a Djiboutian approach to climate and environmental policy that gives particular attention to landscape and to understanding the essential cooperation between humanity and nature.

a5537.speaker: Vinay Talwar, Ambassador of the United Kingdom to Djibouti
a5537.name: Vinay Talwar
a5537.title: Ambassador of the United Kingdom to Djibouti
a5537.speech: At the end of the workshop thanked all the participants who attended the workshop on climate change, humanity and nature; he also urged participants to take the opportunity to ask questions about climate change and the best way to raise awareness among our populations on this theme.

a5655.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a5655.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a5655.speech: Has announced a donation of 100,000 doses of Anthrax vaccine to support the Government of Ghana and the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation in their efforts to protect Ghanaians and livestock from the threat of Anthrax.

a5655.speaker: Kimberly Rosen, Mission Director of USAID/Ghana
a5655.name: Kimberly Rosen
a5655.title: Mission Director of USAID/Ghana
a5655.speech: Made the announcement at the launch of Ghana's first Anthrax vaccination campaign at Kpallaung; emphasised the importance of preventing anthrax outbreaks through regular vaccination campaigns, highlighting the positive impact that healthier animals can have on human safety and potential revenue generation for the Veterinary Services Department; emphasised the importance of public-private partnerships in ensuring the efficient distribution of vaccines: “USAID is partnering with UN Food and Agriculture Organisation to provide technical support for the campaign and to monitor throughout Northern Ghana, and we are also working with FAO to monitor slaughterhouses in order to prioritise a more comprehensive support package to facilities. We are also working to accelerate social behavior change project to create awareness to spread the need to vaccinate animals.”

a5655.speaker: Dr. Benita Anderson, Deputy Director, Veterinary Services Department
a5655.name: Dr. Benita Anderson
a5655.title: Deputy Director, Veterinary Services Department
a5655.speech: Said the success of this campaign relies not only on the vaccines distributed but also on the collective effort and dedication of every individual involved. She urged all stakeholders in beneficiary areas to forge ahead and prioritise the health and well-being of its people and livestock: “Veterinary Services Department will soon come out with the vaccination plan for all regions in the five regions of the North. Together, we can eliminate this disease by implementing the vaccination and coming out to support the campaign when it begins.”

a5655.speaker: Hajia Hawa Musah, Northern Regional Director of Agriculture
a5655.name: Hajia Hawa Musah
a5655.title: Northern Regional Director of Agriculture
a5655.speech: Expressed concern about the condition of slaughterhouses, which she said do not even meet local standards; called for urgent action in that regard, encouraging communities to avail their animals when the exercise begins.

a5665.speaker: Luca Crudeli, development professional (LinkedIn post)
a5665.name: Luca Crudeli
a5665.title: development professional (LinkedIn post)
a5665.speech: Said he has been “immersed in development since 2003”, and spoke of “the sense that the moral centre of our work is quietly slipping away” and “the uneasy realisation that development’s humanistic soul might be lost in a shuffle of contracts and strategic scorecards”.

a5665.speaker: InterAction (statement)
a5665.name: InterAction (statement)
a5665.speech: Said, before a hasty rewrite, that these organisations “work tirelessly to save lives and advance US interests globally” ; added that the attack on USaid had suspended “programs that support America’s global leadership and creates dangerous vacuums that China and our adversaries will quickly fill”.

a5665.speaker: Marina Kobzeva, aid worker of nearly two decades
a5665.name: Marina Kobzeva
a5665.title: aid worker of nearly two decades
a5665.speech: Commented on how colleagues from the Global North and the Global South reacted differently to the statement, describing the former bemoaning it as “poor wording, … an honest mistake” while the latter expressed a sense of vindication: “Finally, they are showing their true colours.”

a5665.speaker: US Congressional Budget Office (1997 study)
a5665.name: US Congressional Budget Office (1997 study)
a5665.speech: Found that foreign aid played, at best, a marginal role in promoting economic development and improving human welfare and could even “hinder development depending on the environment in which that aid is used and the conditions under which it is given”.

a5665.speaker: Heba Aly, former CEO of The New Humanitarian news agency
a5665.name: Heba Aly
a5665.title: former CEO of The New Humanitarian news agency
a5665.speech: Noted that at a recent meeting, “some activists from the Global South proved less worried about aid cuts than the donors were in the hope this would force their own leaders to take responsibility & stop depending on aid”.

a5730.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President and Chair of the Global Leaders Network
a5730.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a5730.title: South African President and Chair of the Global Leaders Network
a5730.speech: Issued a call for coordinated global action to safeguard the health and rights of women, children and adolescents, warning that failure to act will have lasting social and economic consequences, and urged governments, donors and civil society to prioritise inclusive health systems and uphold sexual and reproductive rights: “The cost of inaction on these issues will be counted not only in lives lost, but in futures diminished, communities destabilised, and economic opportunities foregone.” ; “Women, children and adolescents must be our priority for they represent the future that we are all working so hard to secure.” ; “Just as every avoidable death is a policy and administrative failure, every life saved is the result of political will.”

a5730.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President and Chair of the Global Leaders Network
a5730.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a5730.title: South African President and Chair of the Global Leaders Network
a5730.speech: Outlined three urgent priorities for the Global Leaders Network — placing women, children and adolescents at the centre of universal health coverage; increasing investment in health financing through domestic and multilateral mechanisms; and defending sexual and reproductive health rights amid global pushbacks — and also called for innovation in digital health solutions and stronger accountability frameworks; as official development assistance declines and global priorities shift, he stressed that solidarity and sustained investment are essential to building resilient health systems and securing long-term prosperity.

a5730.speaker: Gates Foundation and its partners (recent data)
a5730.name: Gates Foundation and its partners (recent data)
a5730.speech: According to recent data from the Gates Foundation and its partners, sub-Saharan Africa accounts for over half of global maternal deaths, many of which are caused by preventable conditions such as infections, birth complications and unsafe abortions.

a5833.speaker: Dr. Robert Ochola, CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation
a5833.name: Dr. Robert Ochola
a5833.title: CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation
a5833.speech: Reminded us: "Africa can build its own systems and make them world-class."

a5833.speaker: Premier Oiwoh, Managing Director & CEO of NIBSS
a5833.name: Premier Oiwoh
a5833.title: Managing Director & CEO of NIBSS
a5833.speech: Described the NPS as more than just a new platform, emphasizing that it is a foundational investment in Nigeria's financial future. He stressed the importance of building African-led solutions that move beyond legacy frameworks and support free trade through seamless financial movement. He also underscored the value of regulatory collaboration, crediting NIBSS' close partnership with the Central Bank of Nigeria as a key factor in delivering a trusted, efficient and future-ready payment infrastructure.

a5833.speaker: Premier Oiwoh, Managing Director & CEO of NIBSS
a5833.name: Premier Oiwoh
a5833.title: Managing Director & CEO of NIBSS
a5833.speech: "When it comes to uptime, 99.9% isn't good enough. That 0.1% can be critical, even life-altering. For us, the only acceptable KPI is 100%."

a5833.speaker: AfricaNenda Foundation and NIBSS (joint position)
a5833.name: AfricaNenda Foundation and NIBSS (joint position)
a5833.speech: Both AfricaNenda Foundation and NIBSS agree that it is time to dismantle artificial barriers and jurisdictional silos.

a5833.speaker: Musa Jimoh, Director, Payment System Policy at the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
a5833.name: Musa Jimoh
a5833.title: Director, Payment System Policy at the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
a5833.speech: Proposed an Africa Regulators Forum on Instant Payment Systems, a platform that would enable the alignment of standards, foster trust and catalyze collaborative innovation across borders.

a5833.speaker: Chinua Achebe, writer
a5833.name: Chinua Achebe
a5833.title: writer
a5833.speech: Once wrote, "The world is like a Mask dancing. If you want to see it well, you do not stand in one place."

a5923.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5923.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a5923.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5923.speech: Termed the signing of the amendments a strengthening of the historic bilateral ties between the peoples of the United States of America and Liberia, and termed the government and people of the United States a reliable partner to the government and people of Liberia, supporting many aspects of national development ; disclosed that the new amendments to the DOAG will accelerate reforms in health and education and provide essential services to Liberians, and will provide support for programs in three thematic areas: market-driven inclusive economic growth supporting increased job creation, effective and inclusive governance catalyzed through reforms and greater accountability, and a foundation for growth strengthened through a healthy, productive, and educated population; said the activities cut across several sectors, including agriculture, justice, education, and health ; “For a sustainable approach to development, investment in areas of the domestic economy where the most potential can be leveraged to create jobs for our people, especially in the private sector, is critical; this must be done in line with efforts that promote accountability in public sector institutions and ensure resources are managed prudently to benefit all of our people.”

a5923.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning (on behalf of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr.)
a5923.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a5923.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning (on behalf of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr.)
a5923.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the government and people of America for their commitment to the growth of the country.

a5923.speaker: Mark Toner, United States Ambassador to Liberia
a5923.name: Mark Toner
a5923.title: United States Ambassador to Liberia
a5923.speech: Said the ceremony reflects the US government’s shared commitment to advancing Liberia’s development and strengthening the bonds of cooperation between the two nations ; intimated that since the launch of the US$640 million five-year Development Objective Agreement in May 2020, significant strides have been made that have necessitated the addition of the US$114.4 million, making the total contribution to date US$489 million; termed the signing of the amendments a new step on Liberia’s path to growth and prosperity ; “This funding represents more than just financial support; it reflects our steadfast commitment and investment in Liberia’s future” ; disclosed that USAID will provide training for teachers, deliver health commodities to communities in need, and expand economic opportunities in agriculture, and said the US and Liberian governments will ensure that every dollar contributes to a sustainable positive outcome for the Liberian people.

a5923.speaker: Mark Toner, United States Ambassador to Liberia
a5923.name: Mark Toner
a5923.title: United States Ambassador to Liberia
a5923.speech: “As we embark on this new chapter, we must also acknowledge the challenges that remain, including corruption and capacity constraints. Together we must reinforce existing structures needed to address these issues.”

a6432.speaker: Viktor Orban, Hungarian Prime Minister
a6432.name: Viktor Orban
a6432.title: Hungarian Prime Minister
a6432.speech: Rejects the ad hoc text on the strategy of support for Ukraine, leaving only 26 member states to approve it ; had threatened to veto the strategic lines of support for Ukraine, being aligned with Donald Trump's policy and on good terms with Vladimir Putin.

a6432.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
a6432.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a6432.title: President of the European Commission
a6432.speech: On Tuesday presented a major EU plan intended to help member states invest massively in their defences ; said that in total this first package of EU measures could leverage amounts of up to 800 billion euros.

a6432.speaker: The Twenty-Seven (EU heads of state and government)
a6432.name: The Twenty-Seven (EU heads of state and government)
a6432.speech: "Took note" of the principle of a new common instrument of 150 billion euros, which the Commission would borrow on the markets at advantageous rates in order to lend to interested member states.

a6432.speaker: Several sources (anonymous)
a6432.name: Several sources (anonymous)
a6432.speech: According to several sources, the identification of these priority armaments is in itself a major European advance.

a6432.speaker: The Twenty-Six (EU member states other than Hungary), annexed text on Ukraine
a6432.name: The Twenty-Six (EU member states other than Hungary)
a6432.title: annexed text on Ukraine
a6432.speech: Write that the main European principles for a possible peace negotiation are affirmed "firmly," including the territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders: no negotiation on Ukraine without Ukraine; no negotiation touching on Europe's security without involving Europe; any truce or ceasefire can only take place within a process leading to a comprehensive peace agreement; that agreement must be accompanied by "credible and robust" security guarantees to deter future Russian aggression ; also call for increased financial support to Ukraine and for accelerating the disbursement of the 30.6 billion euros already planned for this year.

a6432.speaker: Robert Fico, Slovak Prime Minister
a6432.name: Robert Fico
a6432.title: Slovak Prime Minister
a6432.speech: Had also raised the threat of a refusal, being mainly worried about his country's energy supply now that it is deprived of the Russian gas that transited through Ukraine; a paragraph on this subject was added calling for a solution to be sought.

a6481.speaker: World Health Organization
a6481.name: World Health Organization
a6481.speech: Categorises prevalence of vitamin A deficiency of 2-9% as mild; 10-19% as moderate and over 20% as severe.

a6481.speaker: HyeJin Lee’s study, ‘The status of Uganda’s food-based vitamin A deficiency mitigation strategies’ (African Journal of Food Agriculture, Nutrition and Development, April 22 issue)
a6481.name: HyeJin Lee’s study
a6481.title: ‘The status of Uganda’s food-based vitamin A deficiency mitigation strategies’ (African Journal of Food Agriculture, Nutrition and Development, April 22 issue)
a6481.speech: Concluded that vitamin A deficiency is a public health threat to Uganda, particularly to children; that much effort has been made by the Ugandan government and international agencies to ameliorate VAD with multiple interventions; but that insufficiency of reliable VAD-relevant data and documents makes it difficult to identify evidential grounds for VAD interventions and gauge their progress. It found it unclear whether any positive or negative changes occurred over the years, while living in rural areas and being male consistently increased VAD risks, and the most recent 2016 data hinted at a positive change.

a6481.speaker: ‘Fortification Assessment Coverage Tool (FACT) Survey in Uganda, 2015’ report (released 2017) by the Ministry of Health and the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), with technical support from the US CDC and Makerere University
a6481.name: ‘Fortification Assessment Coverage Tool (FACT) Survey in Uganda
a6481.title: 2015’ report (released 2017) by the Ministry of Health and the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), with technical support from the US CDC and Makerere University
a6481.speech: Found only about 55% of the oil-consuming population were getting the fortified oil, and that fortified maize flour reached less than 7% of households using maize flour.

a6481.speaker: ‘The State of Maize Flour Fortification in Uganda’ report of 2018, United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a6481.name: ‘The State of Maize Flour Fortification in Uganda’ report of 2018
a6481.title: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a6481.speech: Concluded that enforcement of national policies on food fortification needs to be improved; says the majority of maize millers that are required to fortify by law are not currently fortifying, yet they face no consequence, so there is no incentive to change, and that increasing monitoring and enforcement is key to motivating maize millers to adopt fortification; adds that there is a need for further clarification of national standards given confusion around the national policy (some millers assumed fortification is mandatory for those who actually produce 20 MT or more per day, whereas the standard applies to millers with the capacity to produce 20 MT or more per day); notes millers are currently using two different standards for fortification, one according to US:EAS standards for national consumption and one for export for humanitarian purposes, which is difficult for enforcement and quality assurance, and that millers must be educated on fortification standards to increase compliance with mandatory fortification standards as well as QA/QC measures.

a6481.speaker: Ugandan government
a6481.name: Ugandan government
a6481.speech: Has expressed its political commitment to address vitamin A deficiency.

a6523.speaker: Albert Mwiinga, Atwaambe Initiative interim chairperson
a6523.name: Albert Mwiinga
a6523.title: Atwaambe Initiative interim chairperson
a6523.speech: Speaking when he called on Chief Cooma, said the organisation believes in providing a platform where farmers and experts interact for the growth of farming ; “This is a response to climatic changes that we are seeing, to try and come up with innovations that will help the farmers to remain resilient and productive.”

a6523.speaker: Chief Cooma, traditional leader (Choma district)
a6523.name: Chief Cooma
a6523.title: traditional leader (Choma district)
a6523.speech: Welcomed the project, saying he has the munsangu tree in his field, which has enabled him to have good yields despite the drought.

a6652.speaker: Government of Sudan
a6652.name: Government of Sudan
a6652.speech: Has announced plans to shut down operations and evacuate workers from the Heglig oil fields following recent attacks by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

a6652.speaker: Sudan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (statement released on August 30 by the state-owned news agency SUNA)
a6652.name: Sudan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (statement released on August 30 by the state-owned news agency SUNA)
a6652.speech: Said the government may be forced to suspend operations to ensure the safety of its workers ; noted that the attacks not only harm Sudan's national interests but also impact the Republic of South Sudan and the foreign companies that depend on the Heglig area for oil exports.

a6652.speaker: Dr. Fadul Mahmoud, Sudan's Petroleum Undersecretary (letter dated August 30, 2025)
a6652.name: Dr. Fadul Mahmoud
a6652.title: Sudan's Petroleum Undersecretary (letter dated August 30, 2025)
a6652.speech: Stated that the ministry can no longer, in good faith, continue to manage the site's operations ; cited attacks on August 26 and August 30, which damaged the airport terminal in Heglig and caused shrapnel to hit a basecamp, leading to panic among staff, and said that as a result the ministry has reduced the on-site workforce to a minimum.

a6652.speaker: Government of South Sudan
a6652.name: Government of South Sudan
a6652.speech: As of this report, has not commented on the development.

a6751.speaker: Office of President Cyril Ramaphosa / The Presidency of South Africa (statement)
a6751.name: Office of President Cyril Ramaphosa / The Presidency of South Africa (statement)
a6751.speech: In a statement released on Saturday, described the US decision to expel South Africa's ambassador as "regrettable" and urged both countries to uphold established diplomatic norms, while reaffirming Pretoria's commitment to maintaining a cooperative relationship with Washington: "The Presidency has noted the regrettable expulsion of South Africa's Ambassador to the United States of America, Mr. Ebrahim Rasool." ; "The Presidency urges all relevant and impacted stakeholders to maintain the established diplomatic decorum in their engagement with the matter."

a6751.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6751.name: Marco Rubio
a6751.title: US Secretary of State
a6751.speech: Announced the expulsion on Friday and labelled Rasool a "race-baiting politician" with views hostile to President Donald Trump.

a6751.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6751.name: Donald Trump
a6751.title: US President
a6751.speech: Froze US aid to Pretoria last month, citing concerns over land reform policies that he claimed allowed the seizure of land from white farmers, and invited South African farmers to settle in the US, alleging that their government was "confiscating" their land.

a6751.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South Africa's expelled Ambassador to the United States
a6751.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a6751.title: South Africa's expelled Ambassador to the United States
a6751.speech: A former anti-apartheid activist and veteran diplomat, has yet to comment on his expulsion.

a7086.speaker: Émeric Tokoudagba, Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.name: Émeric Tokoudagba
a7086.title: Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.speech: Said the power cuts are due to three essential factors — the relocation of electrical networks because of road construction, as at Vèdoko; problems on the side of certain suppliers, among them Nigeria; and the ageing of the local electricity transmission and distribution networks — and that this is not load-shedding: “Today, Benin has put in place generating units that make it possible to cover 60% of our electricity demand. Pending the filling of the remaining 40% gap, for which contracts have already been signed and for which the works will start soon, we import electricity from Nigeria and from Ghana. The current crisis being sub-regional, there are moments when our suppliers cannot meet their own needs and are obliged to ration the quantity of electricity they can make available to us.”

a7086.speaker: Émeric Tokoudagba, Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.name: Émeric Tokoudagba
a7086.title: Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.speech: Gave the example of Nigeria, where the electricity regulator recently decided to give priority to the Nigerian population over exports: “That has meant that our imports have steadily fallen over the past few weeks” ; detailed that strikes in the electricity sector in the big neighbour to the east affect Benin, as on 3 June when a walkout by the union of Nigeria's transmission grid operator, the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), caused a deliberate shutdown of their national grid.

a7086.speaker: Émeric Tokoudagba, Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.name: Émeric Tokoudagba
a7086.title: Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.speech: Stressed that thanks to the support of the government, which put the means at SBPE's disposal, the company procured HFO liquid fuel and was thus able to weather the storm resiliently: “Unlike many countries in the sub-region that are going through periods of continuous load-shedding, today in Benin our people have electricity 24/7 for their needs.”

a7086.speaker: Émeric Tokoudagba, Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.name: Émeric Tokoudagba
a7086.title: Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.speech: Said the second reason is internal, with many worksites under way in the country requiring network relocation in places: “If you take the most conspicuous case today, the area of the Vèdoko interchange which is under construction, there is a great deal of network-relocation work which does indeed cause disturbances at certain times (…). Today, underground networks are being built more or less everywhere in the country, and as soon as one of these networks is finished, the old networks have to be cut for hours in order to shift the load onto the new ones.”

a7086.speaker: Émeric Tokoudagba, Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.name: Émeric Tokoudagba
a7086.title: Director General of the Société béninoise de production d'électricité (SBPE)
a7086.speech: Said the last reason is linked to the age of the transmission and distribution networks, which are subject to many breakdowns and to accidents in which lines end up de-energised, and reassured that faced with these disturbances the staff of the Société béninoise d'énergie électrique (SBEE) are fighting day and night to bring effective solutions.

a7192.speaker: Prince Adewole Adebayo, lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.name: Prince Adewole Adebayo
a7192.title: lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.speech: In this interview he criticises the Nigerian government for exploiting citizens, comparing it to colonial rule. He notes the lack of infrastructure and policies needed for productivity as well as government's imposition of heavy taxes hinder global competitiveness, just as tax holidays meant to encourage development have instead become a tool for corruption and mismanagement under the current governance framework.

a7192.speaker: Prince Adewole Adebayo, lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.name: Prince Adewole Adebayo
a7192.title: lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.speech: “One of the tools you need for attracting foreign direct investment is a stable or predictable foreign exchange. But even that is not enough. You need to have respect for contracts, you need to have a rule of law, security, and a good justice system. These are essential because if people are to bring their industry here, they need assurances that their investments are protected. Without these fundamental elements, it becomes difficult to foster an environment where businesses can thrive. That's why, in my approach, I would have focused on creating a stable legal and economic framework to encourage productivity and investment.”

a7192.speaker: Prince Adewole Adebayo, lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.name: Prince Adewole Adebayo
a7192.title: lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.speech: “From a legal standpoint, a tax holiday can be a legitimate economic tool to encourage investment, but in the current governance context, it has become a loophole for corruption and mismanagement. Instead of using tax holidays to genuinely support infrastructure and development, they are often exploited by awarding large contracts to entities that under-deliver on quality, with roads and other public works being poorly constructed. These projects are often overpriced, lacking standardisation, and could have been managed more efficiently at the local government level. The legal and regulatory framework should be strengthened to ensure accountability and proper use of public funds, rather than allowing tax holidays to serve as a cover for financial misconduct.”

a7192.speaker: Prince Adewole Adebayo, lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.name: Prince Adewole Adebayo
a7192.title: lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.speech: “If the government taxes me (I Adebayo), I am ready to pay 50% of my income in tax. I don't mind. After all, in Norway, it is higher than that. But I am spending billions, literally, to power my productive enterprises. But you cannot pauperise us, take all the taxes, and still not be responsible for anything. Anyone who tells you that we should remove subsidy from an underdeveloped economy where productivity is low had F9 in economics. In Nigeria. What is there to incentivise productivity? Nothing.”

a7192.speaker: Prince Adewole Adebayo, lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.name: Prince Adewole Adebayo
a7192.title: lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.speech: On the Renewed Hope Agenda: “when renewal of hope starts with removal of your roof over your head, removal of food from your mouth, removal of support for industry and maintaining normal living. When the method chosen is the most damaging of all the options” - comparing it to a doctor who proposes brain surgery for a cold; he blames three major problems: Buhari's “economic illiteracy and lack of awareness” and constant borrowing, the absence of proper administration that let the subsidy balloon out of proportion, and the failure to grow GDP effectively. He argues the solutions brought forward by Tinubu, Atiku and even Peter Obi - removing the petrol subsidy and floating the currency - “does not make any economic sense”, since petrol is a productive input and Nigeria's foreign exchange supply has not grown in 30 years; foreign direct investment also requires respect for contracts, rule of law, security, a good justice system and lower factor costs. He says the government expanded, spent on “the least productive of items”, yanked off support from the economy, created inflation and then had the CBN governor raise interest rates.

a7192.speaker: Prince Adewole Adebayo, lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.name: Prince Adewole Adebayo
a7192.title: lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.speech: “The problem Paul Volcker had when he was appointed by President Carter as chairman of the Federal Reserve was that Carter had inherited high inflation from Nixon and Ford. He thought the only way to kill high inflation was to raise interest rates because cheap credit was driving it. But our inflation in Nigeria is not driven by cheap credit. In fact, there is not sufficient banking penetration, and the lending capacity of our banks is so small that even regional and community banks overseas have more money than the largest bank in Nigeria.”

a7192.speaker: Prince Adewole Adebayo, lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.name: Prince Adewole Adebayo
a7192.title: lawyer and former SDP presidential candidate
a7192.speech: On whether the mindset of emerging leaders affects productivity in governance: “These people don't want to emerge as leaders. They want to take control of the tap of money. They don't want to lead you because if you are leading, you look back sometimes to see whether your people are following you. You are now being exploited by your own people who are exporting your own money overseas because they want their names to appear as one of the richest persons in town. We need to stop that because we are growing a large population that needs to be productive and express their talent. The essence of government is to back you up.”

a7264.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a7264.name: Kashim Shettima
a7264.title: Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a7264.speech: Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu at the 79th United Nations General Assembly in September 2024, took a cue from Nigeria's 25-year unbroken democratic run in renewing her commitment to democratic principles, accountability, and the rule of law, while expressing concern about the unconstitutional changes of government in the Sahel and other regions, as he urged for the restoration of order and the reaffirmation of democratic norms around the world.

a7264.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a7264.name: Kashim Shettima
a7264.title: Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a7264.speech: Emphasised the importance of peace and security in the quest for sustainable development, especially as violent extremism has continued to threaten lives and the stability of communities across Africa and the world; reaffirmed “Nigeria’s unwavering support for the Palestinian people in their struggle for self-determination and the establishment of a sovereign state alongside Israel, based on a just and lasting two-state solution”; underscored Nigeria's commitment to UN peacekeeping and the establishment of the African Standby Force as a critical instrument for regional security and conflict resolution with international support.

a7264.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a7264.name: Kashim Shettima
a7264.title: Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
a7264.speech: Restated Nigeria's commitment to the transformation of the United Nations Security Council and the need for permanent representation for the African continent on the Council.

a7264.speaker: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria's first Prime Minister
a7264.name: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
a7264.title: Nigeria's first Prime Minister
a7264.speech: In the 1960 speech, laid the foundation for Nigeria's foreign policy, declaring the policy of non-alignment, refusing to join either of the ideological or military blocs at the time, committing to the liberation of all of Africa from the grip of the colonialists, declaring support for African liberation movements, while pledging to uphold the principles of the UN Charter.

a7307.speaker: Alexander Babakov, Deputy Chairman of the State Duma and Chairman of the Expert Council on Development and Support of Comprehensive Partnership with African Countries
a7307.name: Alexander Babakov
a7307.title: Deputy Chairman of the State Duma and Chairman of the Expert Council on Development and Support of Comprehensive Partnership with African Countries
a7307.speech: Emphasized that the issues in media communication between Russia and Africa cannot be resolved without state participation: "We will certainly, at least within the framework of the State Duma, look for mechanisms that would primarily prioritize state influence and create conditions under which our state's information agenda could be implemented. There are many institutes and resources available for this. We need to approach them very carefully and seriously today."

a7307.speaker: Maria Zakharova, official representative of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7307.name: Maria Zakharova
a7307.title: official representative of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7307.speech: Highlighted the existing problems in the media field between Russia and Africa: "The network of correspondents of Russian and African media has the potential to develop, but it is insufficient. There are no accredited African media in Russia. Interaction with local correspondents exists, but African journalists visit Russia episodically, mainly for major events. Against the backdrop of French and English-speaking media influence and a lack of Russian content, the African audience gets a distorted view of Russia and bilateral cooperation."

a7307.speaker: Maria Zakharova, official representative of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7307.name: Maria Zakharova
a7307.title: official representative of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7307.speech: Proposed ways to resolve the issues in establishing media relations: "It is important to continue contacts between Russian and African media. Strengthening cooperation through educational programs, press tours, and major media conferences is essential. Africa's population is 1.5 billion, half of whom are under 20 years old. This is an age when people want to learn, set goals, and break into the world. Modern technologies create an information environment that cannot be overlooked. We have achievements, but we need more."

a7307.speaker: Irina Abramova, Director of the Institute for African Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences
a7307.name: Irina Abramova
a7307.title: Director of the Institute for African Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences
a7307.speech: Made several proposals to develop media relations between Russia and Africa: "It is crucial for journalists to understand Africa to avoid mistakes. We are ready to give lectures and cooperate to improve literacy in covering African topics. In large countries, media should broadcast not only in capitals but also in provinces, addressing educational issues as 50% of Africa's population is under 20 years old." ; "Furthermore, it is important to bring African bloggers to show the reality of Russia and unite efforts to expand the themes and understanding of mutual interests. Africa is young, open to new things, and should not be portrayed only as a poor and hungry territory."

a7307.speaker: Louis Gowend, Chair of the Commission for African Diaspora Relations and Public Relations at the Russia-Africa Club of Lomonosov Moscow State University
a7307.name: Louis Gowend
a7307.title: Chair of the Commission for African Diaspora Relations and Public Relations at the Russia-Africa Club of Lomonosov Moscow State University
a7307.speech: Expressed the viewpoint that Irina Olegovna Abramova's idea of creating a unified information space between Russia and Africa should be implemented.

a7307.speaker: Artur Kureev, Editor-in-Chief of "African Initiative"
a7307.name: Artur Kureev
a7307.title: Editor-in-Chief of "African Initiative"
a7307.speech: Emphasized that it is first necessary to unify all resources and media related to Africa to establish a cohesive agenda; added that a comprehensive strategy and understanding are necessary to determine the most effective way to engage with the African audience, and that it is also crucial to assist the African infrastructure and develop it on a Russian foundation, including technological projects for internet development.

a7307.speaker: Kinfu Zenebe, head of African diasporas
a7307.name: Kinfu Zenebe
a7307.title: head of African diasporas
a7307.speech: Stated that collaboration with media should focus on African media representatives in the Russian Federation; suggested that the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs facilitate accreditation for representatives of African media in the Russian Federation, and that African countries should also be allowed to establish small bureaus in Moscow, which would serve as a strategic step towards strengthening strong diplomatic ties.

a7307.speaker: Clarissa Waidorven, Cameroonian journalist and member of the Globus expert club
a7307.name: Clarissa Waidorven
a7307.title: Cameroonian journalist and member of the Globus expert club
a7307.speech: Highlighted the role of media in strengthening Russian-African ties, emphasizing that coverage of these relations in the global media landscape requires attention to both traditional and new media: "Western media actively influence African narratives by enticing local bloggers. Russia should strategically use media platforms to advance its interests, creating a positive image through media diplomacy."

a7307.speaker: Svyatoslav Shchegolev, Head of African Content Production at RT
a7307.name: Svyatoslav Shchegolev
a7307.title: Head of African Content Production at RT
a7307.speech: Emphasized the broadcasting challenges in delivering the Russian perspective to the audience: "Today in Africa, they are finding new ways to convey information to viewers, sometimes in spite of Western pressure. There is a great deal of attention and willingness to cooperate directly from African media. In several countries, this includes state television channels."

a7307.speaker: Victoria Smorodina, Editor-in-Chief of International Reporters
a7307.name: Victoria Smorodina
a7307.title: Editor-in-Chief of International Reporters
a7307.speech: Provided recommendations for France on "surviving" on the African continent: "France needs to rethink its information warfare strategy in Africa, acknowledging the break from past influence. Instead of opposing pan-African demands, it should support the creation of an independent Africa by developing local media, culture, cinema, and theater." According to the Editor-in-Chief, this approach will help counter the influence of Turkey, the USA, and other powers ; "France's defeat in the information sphere should stimulate the development of a new doctrine that combines cognitive sovereignty defense with offensive tools. Partnerships with private companies, a legal framework, and structures are needed to regulate information operations."

a7307.speaker: Andrey Gromov, Executive Secretary of the Board of the African-Russian Energy Association (AREA)
a7307.name: Andrey Gromov
a7307.title: Executive Secretary of the Board of the African-Russian Energy Association (AREA)
a7307.speech: Summarized the roundtable by presenting the resolution's provisions containing specific recommendations on measures to stimulate Russian-African cooperation in the information sphere: "We know of many business projects that simply fell apart because there wasn't enough coverage. We didn't understand from our side the contribution of the Russian Federation."

a7342.speaker: Representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Niger and K. Samba, head of the WFP office
a7342.name: Representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Niger and K. Samba
a7342.title: head of the WFP office
a7342.speech: They thanked Russia for its contribution to the activities of the World Organization in this country, and stressed that thanks to Russian assistance, it was possible to meet the three-month consumption rate of sunflower oil for urgently needed populations, including refugees.

a7342.speaker: Russian Federation (statement)
a7342.name: Russian Federation (statement)
a7342.speech: "For its part, Russia will continue to provide the necessary humanitarian support to the people of the friendly Republic of Niger."

a7444.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a7444.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a7444.title: President of Somalia
a7444.speech: "The European Union has long stood with Somalia through difficult times, and we are grateful for its unwavering support in our journey toward lasting peace and prosperity," he said during the meeting.

a7459.speaker: Jeremy Awori, Ecobank group CEO
a7459.name: Jeremy Awori
a7459.title: Ecobank group CEO
a7459.speech: Said the pan-African lender is "optimistic" about the prospects for its second half performance, as long as there are no further U.S. tariffs or other global shocks: "We are confident that we will see the business continuing to perform. We have got a diversified business."

a7459.speaker: Jeremy Awori, Ecobank group CEO
a7459.name: Jeremy Awori
a7459.title: Ecobank group CEO
a7459.speech: "Our lending is picking up. We are doing that cautiously because there are still many macroeconomic uncertainties and we don't want to lurch back into NPLs (non-performing loans)."

a7459.speaker: Jeremy Awori, Ecobank group CEO
a7459.name: Jeremy Awori
a7459.title: Ecobank group CEO
a7459.speech: Said Ecobank's cash distribution business has been impacted by U.S. President Donald Trump's move to dismantle the United States Agency for International Development (USAID); Ecobank has also been handling funds for the World Health Organisation, which has also been affected by the USAID cuts; he did not provide data but said the impact was distributed across its many markets, meaning the hit on deposits was not pronounced.

a7459.speaker: Jeremy Awori, Ecobank group CEO
a7459.name: Jeremy Awori
a7459.title: Ecobank group CEO
a7459.speech: "A decision taken by the U.S. against China or against Europe can have a knock-on effect across into our markets. We are very joined up."

a7459.speaker: Jeremy Awori, Ecobank group CEO
a7459.name: Jeremy Awori
a7459.title: Ecobank group CEO
a7459.speech: Said Ecobank doesn't have any near-term geographical expansion plans, although an opening-up Ethiopia could be an exception given its size and potential: "It is never say never, but right now, for the next couple of years, we feel we have enough opportunities where we are."

a7459.speaker: Nedbank, South African bank and Ecobank's biggest shareholder
a7459.name: Nedbank
a7459.title: South African bank and Ecobank's biggest shareholder
a7459.speech: Put its 21.2% stake in the bank up for sale, in part due to concerns it may have had to inject more capital in order to prevent "shareholding dilution".

a7508.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South Africa's President
a7508.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a7508.title: South Africa's President
a7508.speech: said that the Ukraine crisis has caused a price hike in energy and fuel, fertilizers and food in African nations and the rest of the world.

a7508.speaker: African delegation (leaders and senior officials from seven African countries)
a7508.name: African delegation (leaders and senior officials from seven African countries)
a7508.speech: offered a peace proposal that includes unimpeded grain exports through the Black Sea, de-escalation on both sides and enhanced humanitarian aid.

a7508.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a7508.name: Vladimir Putin
a7508.title: Russian President
a7508.speech: said Russia understands the concerns of the international community and is open to constructive dialogue with anyone who wants peace based on the principles of justice and takes into account the legitimate interests of all sides ; "Russia has never refused to negotiate, but the Ukrainian side has announced that it will not conduct any negotiations."

a7508.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a7508.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a7508.title: Ukrainian President
a7508.speech: presented the Ukrainian Peace Formula to the leaders of African countries, noting that it would help to restore the security of Ukraine and other states that were affected by the crisis.

a7508.speaker: Antonio Guterres, United Nations Secretary-General
a7508.name: Antonio Guterres
a7508.title: United Nations Secretary-General
a7508.speech: praised the efforts of the African leaders who headed to Russia and Ukraine to promote peace and end the crisis, noting that he always encourages all endeavors related to it.
